annals.noTell: No tell read yet — watch his hands.
annals.title: Annals of the Table
apoc.defeat: The wind blew this page back where it came from.
apoc.history: This page is not entered into the histories.
apoc.name: Apocrypha
apoc.note: The Writer's note: no final draft, no final hand.
apoc.omen.0: River fog closes in from every side
apoc.omen.1: The Wolf Star has not yet fallen
apoc.premise: This page is not in the record. It belongs to tonight alone.
apoc.rule.0: What you see on this page is not always real: more false tells, more feints.
apoc.rule.1: Three battles running, your war chest follows you each time.
apoc.rule.2: He gives no answer and takes no offense—Goading is useless here.
apoc.title.7: Scattered Cards in the River Mist
apoc.yeshi: You win this page, and it scatters on the wind—and another is born.
arena.baimenlou.brief.battle.loss: 'You bind too tight — I beg a moment's slack!' — this time, the one bound hand and foot is you.
arena.baimenlou.brief.battle.title: White Gate Tower · The End of the Unmatched
arena.baimenlou.brief.battle.why: The peerless warrior, the statesman's strategist, the iron-disciplined camp-breakers — a force that should never have lost.
arena.baimenlou.brief.battle.win: Their old habit of fighting each man for himself — you turned it into a fatal wound. The wind at the White Gate Tower blew elsewhere.
arena.baimenlou.brief.era: Third Year of Jian'an · Cao Cao Besieges Xiapi
arena.baimenlou.brief.lead: Atop the White Gate Tower, Lü Bu begged to surrender. Liu Bei sealed his fate with one line: 'Have you forgotten what happened with Ding Jianyang and Dong Zhuo?'
arena.baimenlou.brief.name: Below the White Gate Tower
arena.baimenlou.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Lü Bu / Romance, Chapter 19
arena.baimenlou.btitle: White Gate Tower · The End of the Unmatched

arena.baiyi.brief.battle.loss: They saw you out with perfect courtesy: "Fierce winds at Lukou. The honored guest should head home early."
arena.baiyi.brief.battle.title: Jiangling · White Robes at the Oars
arena.baiyi.brief.battle.why: One feigned illness, one feigned weakness. Lü Meng and Lu Xun staged a grand performance—and built the stage right in front of you.
arena.baiyi.brief.battle.win: You saw through every show of weakness. This time, the white-robed boats never reached the shore.
arena.baiyi.brief.era: Twenty-Fourth Year of Jian'an · Jing Province Changes Hands
arena.baiyi.brief.lead: Merchant boats, white-robed oarsmen—the watchtowers saw nothing. By dawn, Jingzhou had changed its banners.
arena.baiyi.brief.name: Crossing the River in White
arena.baiyi.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Lü Meng / Romance, Chapter 75
arena.baiyi.era: Twenty-Fourth Year of Jian'an · Jing Province Changes Hands
arena.baiyi.lead: Merchant ships in white robes worked their oars; the beacon towers noticed nothing. When the morning came, Jing Province had already changed its banners.
arena.baiyi.loss: They courteously see you out: "The wind at Lukou is strong. The honored guest had best return early."
arena.baiyi.name: Crossing the River in White
arena.baiyi.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Lü Meng / Romance, Chapter Seventy-Five
arena.baiyi.why: One feigns illness, the other feigns weakness. Lü Meng and Lu Xun staged a grand play together—and built the stage right in front of you.
arena.baiyi.win: You saw through every feigned weakness. The white-robed ships did not make it ashore this time.
arena.chencang.brief.battle.loss: "Go home," he said, hand on his sword atop the wall, not even the hem of his robe disturbed.
arena.chencang.brief.battle.title: Chencang · The City of Twenty Days
arena.chencang.brief.battle.why: Beneath the walls of Chencang, attacker and defender trade places. Every push you make meets his fortifications.
arena.chencang.brief.battle.win: You found a crack in the wall. Chencang finally opened a gate.
arena.chencang.brief.era: 2nd year of Taihe · Zhuge Liang's second campaign from Qishan
arena.chencang.brief.lead: Siege ladders, battering rams, fire arrows, tunnels—Hao Zhao held Chencang with barely a thousand men for over twenty days, and Zhuge Liang went home empty-handed.
arena.chencang.brief.name: The Iron Wall of Chencang
arena.chencang.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Cao Zhen (with the affair of Hao Zhao) / Romance, Chapter 97

arena.fengyi.brief.battle.loss: The two lower their halberds and join forces for now—to deal with the outsider first.
arena.fengyi.brief.battle.title: Fengyi Pavilion · The Halberd and the Chain
arena.fengyi.brief.battle.why: Foster father and foster son at one table, each with his own designs. You sit between them: Dong Zhuo's greed and Lü Bu's killing intent both point at you.
arena.fengyi.brief.battle.win: The chain scheme is complete. Father and son are sundered, and the wealth of Meiwu and the edge of the halberd both fall into your hands.
arena.fengyi.brief.era: Third Year of Chuping · Weiyang Palace, Chang'an
arena.fengyi.brief.lead: By the Fengyi Pavilion, Diao Chan stood like a thin strip of water, holding foster father and foster son apart. The sky-piercing halberd was already outside the pavilion.
arena.fengyi.brief.name: Two Shadows at Fengyi
arena.fengyi.brief.ruleText: Seeing is not believing: in this game, fake tells count double.
arena.fengyi.brief.source: Book of the Later Han: Biography of Lü Bu / Romance, Chapter Eight
arena.fengyi.btitle: Fengyi Pavilion · The Halberd and the Chain
arena.fengyi.lead: By Fengyi Pavilion, Diaochan stands like a narrow strip of water, dividing foster father and foster son. The sky-piercing halberd is already outside the pavilion.
arena.fengyi.loss: The two lower their halberds and join forces for now—to deal with you, the outsider, first.
arena.fengyi.name: Two Shadows at Fengyi
arena.fengyi.ruleText: Seeing is not always believing: in this round, tell feints are doubled.
arena.fengyi.source: Book of the Later Han, Biography of Lü Bu / Romance, Chapter 8
arena.fengyi.why: Foster father and son share a table, each with his own designs. You sit between them: Dong Zhuo's greed and Lü Bu's bloodlust both aim at you.
arena.fengyi.win: The chain scheme works. Father and son turn from each other, and the wealth of Mei and the edge of the halberd all fall to you.
arena.ganlu.brief.battle.loss: Jia Chong flicks his sleeve. "A fool—and you'd speak of cards?" Your fate is little better than that of the emperor.
arena.ganlu.brief.battle.title: The Southern Gate · A Passerby's Heart
arena.ganlu.brief.battle.why: The young emperor's blood is still wet. The blade that killed a sovereign and the hand behind it invite you to their table.
arena.ganlu.brief.battle.win: You outlived them all at their own game. This time, Cheng Ji's blade fell on his own.
arena.ganlu.brief.era: Fifth Year of Ganlu · The Palace Coup of Luoyang
arena.ganlu.brief.lead: "Sima Zhao's heart—every passerby knows it." Cao Mao drew his sword and rose. He died beneath the Southern Gate.
arena.ganlu.brief.name: The Ganlu Incident
arena.ganlu.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Annals of the Three Young Emperors / Book of Jin, Annals of Emperor Wen

arena.guandu.brief.battle.loss: Yuan Shao claps his hands and laughs: 'Numbers are justice!' — his luck this time really was better than the histories record.
arena.guandu.brief.battle.title: Guandu · One Fire Against a Hundred Thousand
arena.guandu.brief.battle.why: Hebei has the men and the land. At the table they press you down one voice at a time. All you hold is a single torch labeled 'grain.'
arena.guandu.brief.battle.win: The fire at Wuchao was yours. The fortunes of a family four generations in office scattered across this table.
arena.guandu.brief.era: Fifth Year of Jian'an · Yuan and Cao's Decisive Battle
arena.guandu.brief.lead: A hundred thousand against thirty thousand, and the supply lines hopelessly lopsided. Cao Cao burned Wuchao, and Yuan Shao's great house collapsed overnight.
arena.guandu.brief.name: Standoff at Guandu
arena.guandu.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Annals of Emperor Wu / Romance, Chapter 30

arena.guijin.brief.battle.loss: The iron chains sank; the tower ships broke the waves. The tide took your last chip.
arena.guijin.brief.battle.title: Shitou Fortress · A Banner of Surrender
arena.guijin.brief.battle.why: Iron chains across the Yangtze could not hold the tower ships. The divided realm was at last made one. The three names that close the story wait for you at this table.
arena.guijin.brief.battle.win: You stopped the tower ship on the river. History's final chapter kept one more page for you.
arena.guijin.brief.era: First Year of Taikang · The Three Kingdoms Yield to Jin
arena.guijin.brief.lead: "Wang Jun's tower ships came down from Yizhou; the kingly aura of Jinling dimmed and died." A single banner of surrender rose over Shitou — and the Three Kingdoms came to their end.
arena.guijin.brief.name: Wang Jun's Tower Ships
arena.guijin.brief.source: Book of Jin: Biography of Wang Jun / Romance, Chapter 120

arena.huainan.brief.battle.loss: The night before the city fell, they broke your camp instead. The wind over Huainan has not changed.
arena.huainan.brief.battle.title: Shouchun · Three Rebels in One City
arena.huainan.brief.battle.why: The three rebel commanders have braided themselves into one rope — and this time, the gates of Shouchun did not open.
arena.huainan.brief.battle.win: "So much for the Sima clan's mandate of Heaven." On the wall, they raised a cup to your war chest.
arena.huainan.brief.era: Second Year of Zhengyuan · Huainan in Flames
arena.huainan.brief.lead: Three uprisings at Shouchun, three suppressions by the Sima clan. The brightest blade was Wen Yang, eighteen years old, charging the lines alone.
arena.huainan.brief.name: The Three Rebellions of Huainan
arena.huainan.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Guanqiu Jian / Book of Jin: Annals of Emperor Jing
arena.huainan.btitle: Shouchun · Three Rebels in One City

arena.huarong.brief.battle.loss: "Guan's blade does not cut down a beaten army." He steps aside—without once looking at you.
arena.huarong.brief.battle.title: Huarong Trail · Whether the Blade Falls
arena.huarong.brief.battle.why: The fires of Red Cliffs have died, but the road at Huarong is still blocked. Whether that blade falls, even Lord Guan himself is betting.
arena.huarong.brief.battle.win: You take the pot. The blade is lowered, the road opens—and this act of honor is known to all under heaven.
arena.huarong.brief.era: Thirteenth Year of Jian'an · After the Battle of Red Cliffs
arena.huarong.brief.lead: On a muddy trail, Cao Cao's broken remnant is down to twenty-seven riders. The one who blocks the way, blade drawn, is Guan Yunchang—the man who owes him a debt of kindness.
arena.huarong.brief.name: The Narrow Path at Huarong
arena.huarong.brief.source: Romance, Chapter 50 · Guan Yu Frees Cao Cao at Huarong

arena.jiangdong.brief.battle.loss: "Leave your war chest." Zhou Tai parts his robe, and twelve scars glimmer at once in the lamplight.
arena.jiangdong.brief.battle.title: Jiangdong · Seven of the Twelve Tiger Ministers
arena.jiangdong.brief.battle.why: "Jiangdong breeds tiger ministers." Seven sit around the table, three hundred years between them, a hundred scars.
arena.jiangdong.brief.battle.win: The seven tigers rise. Sun Quan unclasps his sword and offers it two-handed: "Stake the scabbard. Dare you come again?"
arena.jiangdong.brief.era: Jian'an to Wufeng · The Jiangdong Foundation
arena.jiangdong.brief.lead: Cheng Pu, Huang Gai, Han Dang—veterans of three reigns; Zhou Tai, twelve wounds borne for his lord; Gan Ning of the brocade sails, Ling Tong the peerless gentleman, Ding Feng who cut down foes with short blades through the snow. Twelve names in all; seven take seats tonight.
arena.jiangdong.brief.name: Tigers of Jiangdong
arena.jiangdong.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biographies of Cheng, Huang, Han, Jiang, Zhou, Chen, Dong, Gan, Ling, Xu, Pan, and Ding

arena.kongcheng.brief.battle.loss: He rises, flicking his sleeve. "Bluff and bluster—and you dare teach a master his craft." The gates close behind him.
arena.kongcheng.brief.battle.title: West City · One Zither Against a Hundred and Fifty Thousand
arena.kongcheng.brief.battle.why: A hundred and fifty thousand men below the wall, one zither above. He bets you have an ambush inside; you bet he won't dare come in.
arena.kongcheng.brief.battle.win: The string never snaps, and the army withdraws. You wagered on his suspicion—and won.
arena.kongcheng.brief.era: Sixth Year of Jianxing · Zhuge Liang's First March from Qishan
arena.kongcheng.brief.lead: The gates stand wide open, and Kongming plays his zither atop the wall. Sima Yi's hundred and fifty thousand men halt on a single string.
arena.kongcheng.brief.name: The Zither on the Empty Wall
arena.kongcheng.brief.source: Romance, Chapter 95 · The Empty City Stratagem (Pei's commentary, quoting Guo Chong's three accounts)

arena.nanman.brief.battle.loss: The rattan-armor fire burned the wrong way. This time, the one "released" is you.
arena.nanman.brief.battle.title: Coiled Snake Valley · Where the Seven Captures Happened
arena.nanman.brief.battle.why: The tribal warriors come at you in waves: the tough, the soft, the tricky, the simple. It's not one hand you must win—it's all of Nanzhong.
arena.nanman.brief.battle.win: "The southerners will never rebel again!" Meng Huo and his host bow in submission. Your "seven captures," done in a single table.
arena.nanman.brief.era: Third Year of Jianxing · Zhuge Liang's Southern Expedition
arena.nanman.brief.lead: Seven times released, seven times taken. Meng Huo wept: "The southerners will never rebel again!" The fire of the rattan-armored troops burned Coiled Snake Valley for three days.
arena.nanman.brief.name: Seven Captures of the Southern Campaign
arena.nanman.brief.source: Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapter 90 · Seven Captures, Seven Releases
arena.nanman.btitle: Coiled Snake Valley · Where Seven Were Taken
arena.nanman.era: 3rd year of Jianxing · Zhuge Liang's southern campaign
arena.nanman.lead: Seven times released, seven times taken; Meng Huo wept: "The southerners will never rise again!" The fire of the rattan-armored troops burned Coiled Snake Valley for three days.
arena.nanman.loss: The rattan-armored troops' fire burned the wrong way. This time, the one "released" was you.
arena.nanman.name: Seven Times Spared in Nanzhong
arena.nanman.source: Romance, Chapter 90 · Captured seven times, released seven times
arena.nanman.why: The tribal warriors come at you in waves: the hard, the soft, the cunning, the simple. What you must win is not one hand, but all of Nanzhong.
arena.nanman.win: "The southerners will never rise again!" Meng Huo and his host bowed in submission. Your "seven captures"—done in a single sitting.
arena.qishui.brief.battle.loss: Pang De's coffin still stands; your war chest sank first.
arena.qishui.brief.battle.title: Fancheng · Autumn Rain and the Seven Armies
arena.qishui.brief.battle.why: The flood washed away seven camps—and washed up two kinds of men: those who surrendered, and those who would not retreat a step.
arena.qishui.brief.battle.win: The flood is on your side. Thirty thousand captives and one coffin, all left behind in the great water.
arena.qishui.brief.era: Twenty-Fourth Year of Jian'an · Guan Yu's Northern Campaign
arena.qishui.brief.lead: Autumn rains fell without end, and the Han River swelled. Yu Jin's seven armies were all lost; Pang De carried his coffin into battle, and when his arrows ran out he fought on with the blade.
arena.qishui.brief.name: Drowning the Seven Armies
arena.qishui.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Guan Yu / Romance, Chapter Seventy-Four

arena.ruxu.brief.battle.loss: "Hold the walls. Ten more days." Cao Cao sips his tea, unhurried, and your war chest runs dry in the river wind.
arena.ruxu.brief.battle.title: Ruxu · Four Hundred Thousand Hold Fast
arena.ruxu.brief.battle.why: An army at your gates that will not move—Cao Cao is waiting for the other side to break first. Xu Huang's camp goes up at your flank before anything else.
arena.ruxu.brief.battle.win: You are not the one who broke first. The commander of four hundred thousand pushes back his cards and concedes.
arena.ruxu.brief.era: Jian'an 18 · Cao Cao's Campaign Against Wu
arena.ruxu.brief.lead: "He should have been my son, this Sun Zhongmou." Cao Cao brought four hundred thousand to the river; Sun Quan held him with seventy thousand, and for a month no battle came.
arena.ruxu.brief.name: Standoff at Ruxu
arena.ruxu.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, 'Biography of the Lord of Wu' / Romance, Chapter 61

arena.sanying.brief.battle.loss: "Third brother, stand down." Liu Bei holds back the surging Zhang Fei. "This one is not Lü Bu."
arena.sanying.brief.battle.title: Hulao Pass · One Against Three
arena.sanying.brief.battle.why: Three sworn brothers together—even Lü Bu had to fall back. Today all three sit at one table, to weigh what you alone are worth.
arena.sanying.brief.battle.win: You weathered the Peach Garden trio's charge after charge. That feat deserves a place in any tattered scroll.
arena.sanying.brief.era: Chuping 1 · The Eighteen Lords Against Dong Zhuo
arena.sanying.brief.lead: Before Hulao Pass, Liu, Guan, and Zhang rode out together. Lü Bu could not hold them off, and fled dragging his halberd behind him.
arena.sanying.brief.name: Three Heroes, One Table
arena.sanying.brief.source: Romance, Chapter 5 · Three Heroes Fight Lü Bu
arena.sanying.era: Chuping 1 · The Eighteen Lords Against Dong Zhuo

arena.shangfanggu.brief.battle.loss: A "great rain" snuffed out your assault. Sima Yi wiped the soot from his face: "Heaven's will."
arena.shangfanggu.brief.battle.title: Shangfang Valley · The Rain That Never Came
arena.shangfanggu.brief.battle.why: Four of them clawed their way out of that death-trap at the valley's floor. That survivor's ferocity is all aimed at you.
arena.shangfanggu.brief.battle.win: This time, the rain did not fall. The fire of Shangfang Valley burned to the end.
arena.shangfanggu.brief.era: 12th year of Jianxing · Zhuge Liang's sixth campaign from Qishan
arena.shangfanggu.brief.lead: Fire rose in the valley; Sima Yi and his sons wept in each other's arms. Then the heavens opened and a great rain put out the last of the flames.
arena.shangfanggu.brief.name: Rain at Shangfang Valley
arena.shangfanggu.brief.source: Romance, Chapter 103 · Sima Yi trapped at Shangfang Valley
arena.shangfanggu.btitle: Shangfang Valley · The Rain That Never Came

arena.shenting.brief.battle.loss: He picks up your weapon for you: 'Train ten years, then come back to the ridge.'
arena.shenting.brief.battle.title: Shenting Ridge · After the Halberds Snapped
arena.shenting.brief.battle.why: One rider against one rider, till the banner poles broke. Taishi Ci flings aside his broken halberd and bids you meet him on the ridge to settle it in earnest.
arena.shenting.brief.battle.win: A match for a match, a worthy for a worthy. He laughs and hurls down his cup: 'Friends only after a fight!'
arena.shenting.brief.era: First Year of Xingping · Sun Ce Crosses East
arena.shenting.brief.lead: Sun Ce and Taishi Ci met on a narrow path at Shenting Ridge. Halberds snapped, armor split, and the two rolled down the slope still laughing.
arena.shenting.brief.name: Fierce Battle at Shenting
arena.shenting.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Taishi Ci / Romance, Chapter 15
arena.shenting.btitle: Shenting Ridge · After the Halberds Snapped

arena.shezhan.brief.battle.loss: "If you cannot even out-talk us, how will you sway our lord?" Amid the laughter, you were shown out of Chaisang.
arena.shezhan.brief.battle.title: Chaisang · One Tongue Against the Southland
arena.shezhan.brief.battle.why: The Southland's silver tongues have you surrounded. What this hand wins is not war chest—it is the answer to "surrender" or "fight."
arena.shezhan.brief.battle.win: The whole hall fell silent. Zhang Zhao raised his cup first: "Sir, please—for the alliance."
arena.shezhan.brief.era: Jian'an 13 · The Eve of the Sun-Liu Alliance
arena.shezhan.brief.lead: Kongming crossed the river in a single skiff, and twenty-odd men from Zhang Zhao down surrounded him to attack. One lute against a million soldiers.
arena.shezhan.brief.name: Battle of Words
arena.shezhan.brief.source: Romance, Chapter 43 · A War of Words with the Scholars
arena.shezhan.btitle: Chaisang · One Tongue Against the Southland

arena.taodong.brief.battle.loss: The alliance scatters. Each returns to his own camp, leaving you alone to face the Xiliang army.
arena.taodong.brief.battle.title: Suanzao · The Eighteen Lords
arena.taodong.brief.battle.why: Seven lords at one table: the figurehead leader, the grain-grabber Gonglu, Mengde who truly fights, Wentai the vanguard… and you in the very center.
arena.taodong.brief.battle.win: Yuan Shao rises and lifts his cup: "Tomorrow we strike camp—and follow this one's word." The whole campaign against Dong, settled in one game.
arena.taodong.brief.era: 1st year of Chuping · The East of the Pass Rises
arena.taodong.brief.lead: Eighteen lords swore an oath against Dong Zhuo. Yuan Shao led, each with his own scheme—before the wine could cool, the alliance split from within.
arena.taodong.brief.name: Coalition Against Dong Zhuo
arena.taodong.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Annals of Emperor Wu / Romance, Chapter 5
arena.taodong.era: 1st year of Chuping · The East of the Pass Rises

arena.taodong.loss: The alliance scatters. Each returns to his own camp, leaving you alone to face the Xiliang army.

arena.tianshui.brief.battle.loss: "The old general praised me—who are you?" The young man's edge cut into you today.
arena.tianshui.brief.battle.title: Tianshui · First Cry of the Young Qilin
arena.tianshui.brief.battle.why: He saw through Kongming's trick of luring the tiger from the mountain and turned to surround the Shu camp. This round, you face him.
arena.tianshui.brief.battle.win: Kongming was right. Win this round, and even the Chancellor wants to take you as a student.
arena.tianshui.brief.era: 7th year of Jianxing · Jiang Wei joins Han
arena.tianshui.brief.lead: A young man who made even Zhao Yun stumble. Kongming asked in astonishment: there is such a talent here?
arena.tianshui.brief.name: The Qilin of Tianshui
arena.tianshui.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Jiang Wei / Romance, Chapter 93

arena.tingzhu.brief.battle.loss: "Hebei has many worthy men." Behind the screen, Yuan Shao raises his cup. Four spears have taken every coin in your war chest.
arena.tingzhu.brief.battle.title: Jizhou · Four Spears of Hebei
arena.tingzhu.brief.battle.why: Four long spears laid out in a line. Yuan Shao has staked all of Hebei's wealth on this table.
arena.tingzhu.brief.battle.win: The four pillars are broken. The debts of Baima and Yanjin are settled together.
arena.tingzhu.brief.era: Fourth Year of Jian'an · Strife in Hebei
arena.tingzhu.brief.lead: Yan Liang, Wen Chou, Zhang He, Gao Lan — the four sharpest spears in Hebei. The ridgepole, Qu Yi, died early; the four pillars still stand.
arena.tingzhu.brief.name: The Four Pillars of Hebei
arena.tingzhu.brief.source: Romance, Chapter 26 · Four Pillars and a Beam
arena.tingzhu.era: Fourth Year of Jian'an · Strife in Hebei

arena.tongguan.brief.battle.loss: Two long spears press down at once. The wind of Tong Pass collects your war chest on their behalf.
arena.tongguan.brief.battle.title: Tong Pass · After the Beard Was Cut and the Robe Flung
arena.tongguan.brief.battle.why: A father's murder and a lord's defense collide across a card table. Neither of these men can give up half a step.
arena.tongguan.brief.battle.win: The Tiger Fool and the Brocade Horse both turn to you—this bet is worthy of the Wei River's name.
arena.tongguan.brief.era: Sixteenth Year of Jian'an · Battle of Weinan
arena.tongguan.brief.lead: "If that horse-boy lives, I have no place to be buried." Cao Cao cut his beard and flung away his robe; Xu Chu stripped to the waist and fought Ma Chao for over two hundred bouts without a victor.
arena.tongguan.brief.name: Vengeance at Tong Pass
arena.tongguan.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Ma Chao / Romance, Chapter Fifty-Eight
arena.tongguan.btitle: Tong Pass · After the Beard Was Cut and the Robe Flung

arena.tongquetai.brief.battle.loss: Xu Chu slings the robe over his shoulder: "Can't outshoot us, and can't outplay us either?"
arena.tongquetai.brief.battle.title: Bronze Sparrow Terrace · The Robe Hung High
arena.tongquetai.brief.battle.why: The brocade robe hangs above the table. Cao's tiger generals leave their seats in turn—this time it's not arrows being matched, but bets.
arena.tongquetai.brief.battle.win: The robe is yours. The whole hall of tiger generals cups their fists as one: "Your cardcraft earns that robe, sir!"
arena.tongquetai.brief.era: 15th year of Jian'an · The great feast at Bronze Sparrow Terrace
arena.tongquetai.brief.lead: Cao Cao hung a Shu brocade war-robe from a weeping willow. Each general showed his skill, one arrow one feat, all for that single robe.
arena.tongquetai.brief.name: The Bronze Sparrow Robe Contest
arena.tongquetai.brief.source: Romance, Chapter 56 · Cao Cao's great feast at Bronze Sparrow Terrace
arena.tongquetai.btitle: Bronze Sparrow Terrace · The Brocade Hangs High
arena.tongquetai.era: Fifteenth Year of Jian'an · The Grand Feast at Bronze Sparrow
arena.tongquetai.lead: Cao Cao hung a Shu brocade robe from a weeping willow branch, and the generals vied to prove their skill — one arrow, one deed — all for that single robe.
arena.tongquetai.loss: Xu Chu slings the robe over his shoulder: "Can't outshoot us, and can't outplay us either?"
arena.tongquetai.name: The Robe at Bronze Sparrow Terrace
arena.tongquetai.source: Romance, Chapter 56 · Cao Cao's Grand Feast at Bronze Sparrow Terrace

arena.wenjiu.brief.battle.loss: That cup has gone cold. Hua Xiong's laughter is colder than the wind beyond the pass.
arena.wenjiu.brief.battle.title: Sishui Pass · A Cup Still Warm
arena.wenjiu.brief.battle.why: Hua Xiong challenges at the pass, and the coalition holds its breath. You ask only for a cup of hot wine, then rise and leave the tent.
arena.wenjiu.brief.battle.win: The wine is still warm, the pass already broken. The eyes of every lord in that tent are different from now on.
arena.wenjiu.brief.era: Second Year of Chuping · The Eastern Coalition Against Dong Zhuo
arena.wenjiu.brief.lead: Hua Xiong cut down several of the coalition's generals in a row, and no one in the tent dared answer. One man asked for a cup of hot wine, pushed back his bench, and rose—he would drink it on his return; by then it would still be warm.
arena.wenjiu.brief.name: Warm Wine, Slain Hua Xiong
arena.wenjiu.brief.ruleText: Short, fast bout: war chest 600, blinds 15/30, blinds rise fast—while the wine is still warm.
arena.wenjiu.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Sun the Tiger-Slayer / Romance, Chapter 5 — Warm Wine, Slain Hua Xiong

arena.wuguan.brief.battle.loss: "Seize him!" Beacon fires blazed at all five passes. This time, you did not get through.
arena.wuguan.brief.battle.title: The Highway · Five Passes, Six Generals
arena.wuguan.brief.battle.why: Five checkpoints, one after another: waving him through, pressing wine on him, setting fires, demanding his papers—now all become five cutdowns at the table.
arena.wuguan.brief.battle.win: Five passes broken in a row, the Yellow River in sight. You walked this road steadier than Lord Guan himself.
arena.wuguan.brief.era: 5th year of Jian'an · Seal hung up, gold left behind
arena.wuguan.brief.lead: One carriage with his two sisters-in-law, one rider in a cloud of dust. Five passes, six defending generals—none could bar the way of a single word: loyalty.
arena.wuguan.brief.name: Five Passes, a Thousand Li
arena.wuguan.brief.source: Romance, Chapter 27 · Through five passes, six generals slain
arena.wuguan.btitle: The Highway · Five Passes, Six Generals

arena.wuhu.brief.battle.loss: "Nothing more than that." Guan Yu narrows his phoenix eyes. Five divine weapons, and not a single chip left for you.
arena.wuhu.brief.battle.title: Hanzhong · The Five Tigers at Table
arena.wuhu.brief.battle.why: Five Tigers invested, their might shaking the land. Today the five sit at one table to test your strength alone.
arena.wuhu.brief.battle.win: The Five Tigers yield. Huang Zhong strokes his white beard: "My bow bows to you."
arena.wuhu.brief.era: Twenty-Fourth Year of Jian'an · The King of Hanzhong Invests His Generals
arena.wuhu.brief.lead: Guan, Zhang, Zhao, Ma, Huang—Shu Han's five divine weapons, seated at one table. Yide wants to brawl, Yunchang wants to sneer, Zilong wants to hold steady.
arena.wuhu.brief.name: The Five Tiger Generals
arena.wuhu.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biographies of Guan, Zhang, Ma, Huang, and Zhao / Romance, Chapter 73

arena.wuzhang.brief.battle.loss: He pushed his cards aside and rose: "Another hundred days of holding—what of it." Your war chest hit bottom first.
arena.wuzhang.brief.battle.title: Wuzhang Plains · Autumn Wind Against the Iron Wall
arena.wuzhang.brief.battle.why: Kongming sent him women's clothes, and he put them on with a smile. All that patience has now been spent at the table.
arena.wuzhang.brief.battle.win: You outlasted until the autumn wind rose. The Iron Wall across from you cracked for the first time.
arena.wuzhang.brief.era: 12th year of Jianxing · Zhuge Liang's fifth campaign from Qishan
arena.wuzhang.brief.lead: A hundred days of standoff. Sima Yi only defends, never fights. He isn't betting on cards—he's betting you can't outlast the autumn by the Wei River.
arena.wuzhang.brief.name: Autumn Wind at Wuzhang
arena.wuzhang.brief.ruleText: Long game, deep stacks: war chest 2400, blinds rise glacially—this one is about who can outlast.
arena.wuzhang.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Zhuge Liang / Romance, Chapter 103
arena.wuzhang.btitle: Wuzhang Plains · Autumn Wind Against a Solid Wall
arena.wuzhang.era: Twelfth Year of Jianxing · Zhuge Liang's Fifth March from Qishan
arena.wuzhang.lead: A hundred days of standoff, and Sima Yi only defends, never strikes. He isn't betting on cards—he's betting on whether the other man can outlast the autumn by the Wei River.
arena.wuzhang.loss: He pushes his cards away and rises. "Another hundred days of holding—what of it." Your war chest, though, has bottomed out first.
arena.wuzhang.name: Autumn Wind at Wuzhang
arena.wuzhang.ruleText: Long game, deep stacks: war chest 2400, blinds rising very slowly—this one is all about outlasting.
arena.wuzhang.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Zhuge Liang / Romance, Chapter 103
arena.wuzhang.why: Kongming sent him a woman's robes, and he put them on with a smile. All that patience is now spent at the poker table.
arena.wuzhang.win: You endure until the autumn wind rises. The "solid wall" across the river cracks for the first time.
arena.wuzi.brief.battle.loss: Strict military law, no disorder in their ranks. The Five together left you no tell to exploit.
arena.wuzi.brief.battle.title: Ye · The Five Foremost
arena.wuzi.brief.battle.why: The Five sit in array, advancing and retreating as one. A force in strict discipline—even their bluffs come in formation.
arena.wuzi.brief.battle.win: The Five fall together. If Chen Shou rewrote their chapter, he'd have to add your name first.
arena.wuzi.brief.era: Jian'an Era · Cao Wei Military System
arena.wuzi.brief.lead: "When the Founder established these martial deeds, the finest generals of the age were the Five." Chen Shou wrote them in one chapter, and the five share a seat.
arena.wuzi.brief.name: The Five Elite Generals
arena.wuzi.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Commentary on the Biographies of Zhang, Yue, Yu, Zhang, and Xu

arena.xiaoyao.brief.battle.loss: 'Liao comes—!' The shout had barely landed when your rear ranks broke.
arena.xiaoyao.brief.battle.title: Xiaoyao Ford · Eight Hundred Against a Hundred Thousand
arena.xiaoyao.brief.battle.why: 'Liao comes! Liao comes!' — the trio's charge always comes from the direction you least expect.
arena.xiaoyao.brief.battle.win: You held your ground. The legend of eight hundred stopped at the edge of your camp.
arena.xiaoyao.brief.era: Twentieth Year of Jian'an · Battle of Hefei
arena.xiaoyao.brief.lead: Eight hundred men punched through an army of a hundred thousand, and Sun Quan nearly fell captive. 'Zhang Liao halts the crying' — children of Jiangdong dared not weep at night when they heard his name.
arena.xiaoyao.brief.name: On the Xiaoyao Ford
arena.xiaoyao.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Zhang Liao / Romance, Chapter 67
arena.xiaoyao.btitle: Xiaoyao Ford · Eight Hundred Against a Hundred Thousand
arena.xiaoyao.era: Twentieth Year of Jian'an · Battle of Hefei
arena.xiaoyao.lead: Eight hundred men punched through an army of a hundred thousand, and Sun Quan nearly fell captive. 'Zhang Liao halts the crying' — children of Jiangdong dared not weep at night when they heard his name.
arena.xiaoyao.loss: 'Liao comes—!' The shout had barely landed when your rear ranks broke.
arena.xiaoyao.name: On the Xiaoyao Ford
arena.xiaoyao.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Zhang Liao / Romance, Chapter 67
arena.xiaoyao.why: 'Liao comes! Liao comes!' — the trio's charge always comes from the direction you least expect.
arena.xiaoyao.win: You held your ground. The legend of eight hundred stopped at the edge of your camp.
arena.xichuan.brief.battle.loss: "Western Shu is ringed with perilous passes, a thousand li of fertile fields." They raise their cups on the wall and send you back to Jiameng Pass.
arena.xichuan.brief.battle.title: Luo City · Western Shu on the Table
arena.xichuan.brief.battle.why: Veterans, defectors, strategists, turncoats—the whole expedition to Shu is here. What you must win is Western Shu itself.
arena.xichuan.brief.battle.win: Chengdu opens its gates. The war chest from this table will fund another ten years in Shu.
arena.xichuan.brief.era: 19th year of Jian'an · Liu Bei Takes Shu
arena.xichuan.brief.lead: The Fledgling Phoenix died at Fallen Phoenix Slope; Zhang Ren met his fate by the Yan Bridge. Yet Western Shu took the name of Liu in the end—old and new, civil and martial, all seated at one table.
arena.xichuan.brief.name: Seizing Western Shu
arena.xichuan.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of the First Ruler / Romance, Chapter 65
arena.xichuan.btitle: Luo City · Western Shu on the Table
arena.xichuan.era: Nineteenth Year of Jian'an · Liu Bei Pacifies Shu
arena.xichuan.lead: The Fledgling Phoenix died at Fallen Phoenix Slope; Zhang Ren met his end by the Wild Goose Bridge. Yet Western Shu took the name Liu in the end—old hands and new, civil and military, all at one table.
arena.xichuan.loss: "Western Shu is a fortress of passes, a thousand li of fertile fields." They raise their cups on the wall and send you back to Jiameng Pass.
arena.xichuan.name: Seizing Western Shu
arena.xichuan.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of the First Sovereign / Romance, Chapter 65
arena.xichuan.why: Veterans, surrendered officers, the chief strategist, the inside man—the whole staff that entered Shu is here. What you must win is Western Shu itself.
arena.xichuan.win: Chengdu opens its gates. The war chest on this table is enough to fight ten more years in Western Shu.
arena.yanglu.brief.battle.loss: He accepts the wine you sent. "Your game, sir, still lacks a spark."
arena.yanglu.brief.battle.title: The Frontier · Opponents at the Board
arena.yanglu.brief.battle.why: They agreed to speak only of wind and moon, never of arms. But once the chips are on the table, even the closest friends must show their true hand.
arena.yanglu.brief.battle.win: "This round, Hu concedes." He raises his cup, smiling. "Same time next year—so long as we both still stand."
arena.yanglu.brief.era: Eighth Year of Taishi · Wu and Jin at Standoff
arena.yanglu.brief.lead: At war along the border, yet they send each other wine and medicine. Yang Hu and Lu Kang are enemies—and each other's only true friend in this life.
arena.yanglu.brief.name: Yang and Lu
arena.yanglu.brief.source: Book of Jin, Biography of Yang Hu / Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Lu Kang
arena.yanglu.btitle: The Frontier · Opponents at the Board
arena.yanglu.era: Eighth Year of Taishi · Wu and Jin at Standoff
arena.yanglu.lead: At war along the border, yet they send each other wine and medicine. Yang Hu and Lu Kang are enemies—and each other's only true friend in this life.
arena.yanglu.loss: He accepts the wine you sent. "Your game, sir, still lacks a spark."
arena.yanglu.name: Yang and Lu
arena.yanglu.source: Book of Jin, Biography of Yang Hu / Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Lu Kang
arena.yanglu.why: They agreed to speak only of wind and moon, never of arms. But once the chips are on the table, even the closest friends must show their true hand.
arena.yanglu.win: "This round, Hu concedes." He raises his cup, smiling. "Same time next year—so long as we both still stand."
arena.yinping.brief.battle.loss: They came out of the sky. You never even got the beacon lit.
arena.yinping.brief.battle.title: Yinping · Seven Hundred Li of Sheer Cliffs
arena.yinping.brief.battle.why: Father and son, cutting deep with no way back—a cliff behind them, you ahead. Retreat is death; advance means your war chest.
arena.yinping.brief.battle.win: Even a surprise force runs out of road. You cut this narrow pass shut, and the wind over Mianzhu turned.
arena.yinping.brief.era: Fourth Year of Jingyuan · Wei's Conquest of Shu
arena.yinping.brief.lead: Seven hundred li of empty land. They cut a road through the mountains, wrapped themselves in felt, and rolled down the cliffs. The garrison at Jiangyou surrendered without a fight.
arena.yinping.brief.name: The Lone Army at Yinping
arena.yinping.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Deng Ai / Romance, Chapter 117
arena.yinping.btitle: Yinping · Seven Hundred Li of Sheer Cliffs
arena.yinping.era: Fourth Year of Jingyuan · Wei's Conquest of Shu
arena.yinping.lead: Seven hundred li of empty land. They cut a road through the mountains, wrapped themselves in felt, and rolled down the cliffs. The garrison at Jiangyou surrendered without a fight.
arena.yinping.loss: They came down from the sky. You never even had time to light the beacon.
arena.yinping.name: The Lone Army at Yinping
arena.yinping.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Deng Ai / Romance, Chapter 117
arena.yinping.why: Father and son plunge deep with no army behind them—cliffs at their backs, you ahead. Retreat is death; advance, and your war chest is theirs.
arena.yinping.win: Even a surprise force has its limits. You sealed the treacherous pass, and the wind at Mianzhu turned.
arena.zhujiu.brief.battle.loss: "No?" His smile never wavers, but the hand inside his sleeve tightens. Go home and tend your vegetables.
arena.zhujiu.brief.battle.title: Green Plums and Warm Wine · Who Is the Hero
arena.zhujiu.brief.battle.why: The plums are ripe, the little cauldron freshly boiling. Cao Mengde raises a hand and invites you to the table: who is the hero? The cards will tell.
arena.zhujiu.brief.battle.win: He drains his cup in one go. "A hero indeed. This stake, I concede."
arena.zhujiu.brief.era: Fourth Year of Jian'an · Xu Capital
arena.zhujiu.brief.lead: "The only heroes in this world are you and I." That was the table where the thunder made him drop his chopsticks. Now it holds war chests instead.
arena.zhujiu.brief.name: Wine and Heroes
arena.zhujiu.brief.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Annals of the Former Lord / Romance, Chapter 21
arena.zhujiu.btitle: Green Plums and Boiled Wine · Who Is the Hero
arena.zhujiu.lead: 'The heroes of this world are you and I alone.' At that table, where the thunderclap made him drop his chopsticks, the stakes are now laid.
arena.zhujiu.loss: "No?" His smile never wavers, but the hand inside his sleeve tightens. Go home and tend your vegetables.
arena.zhujiu.name: Boiling Wine, Judging Heroes
arena.zhujiu.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of the First Sovereign / Romance, Chapter 21
arena.zhujiu.why: The green plums are ripe, the little cauldron freshly boiling. Cao Mengde raises his hand and bids you sit: who is the hero—let the cards say.
arena.zhujiu.win: He drains his cup: 'A hero indeed. This bet, Cao concedes.'
banner.allLeft: The heroes have all left the table
banner.allLeft.sub: He throws down his staff and goes
banner.autumnWind.sub: He has waited for this, and it has come.
banner.loseButContinue.sub: This round was never about the last one.
battle.qiqinSub: Catch him, and let him go.
battle.resultLossSub: The war chest ran dry; this stand was lost.
battle.resultWinSub: Their war chest is empty — you march on with this table’s spoils.
brief.baidicheng.adaptation: This chapter pits you against 'Fate: Deep Illness.' It does not claim a card game can cure disease; it asks whether, in limited time, dying words can turn from probing back to honesty.
brief.baidicheng.boss.loss: The long night at Yong'an Palace ends, and the original entrustment arrives as recorded. The words left unspoken become the weight Zhuge Liang carries in every decision he makes alone.
brief.baidicheng.boss.title: Baidicheng · Words Against Fate
brief.baidicheng.boss.why: Deep illness means to take away the time for speech. You must win a moment honest enough that Liu Bei no longer lays the whole realm on Zhuge Liang alone.
brief.baidicheng.boss.win: The will is rewritten; the heir and the regent each bear their own charge. Liu Bei wins time among the living, and the later pages of the southern campaign and the northern expeditions change with it.
brief.baidicheng.lead: After Yiling, the fires receded, but the wasting within caught up. Your opponent this time is no famed general, but time itself—the one thing no one can frighten away.
brief.baidicheng.record: Gravely ill at Yong'an Palace, Liu Bei entrusts Liu Shan to Zhuge Liang, with Li Yan as deputy, and then dies. The Baidicheng entrustment holds both trust and the heavy reality of a transfer of power.
brief.baidicheng.skirmish.loss: Suspicion seals the palace gates first; the will is not yet finished before each faction wields it as a weapon. The entrustment reduces to a struggle for power.
brief.baidicheng.skirmish.title: Yong'an Palace · Night Guard
brief.baidicheng.skirmish.why: Rumors of the will have the palace guards on edge. A single misunderstanding could turn the final entrustment into a palace coup over a dying man's command.
brief.baidicheng.skirmish.win: The gates and the medicine route hold secure. In a night without the sound of steel, Liu Bei speaks plainly, and Zhuge Liang and the young heir share the same table.
brief.baidicheng.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biographies of the Former Lord and Zhuge Liang
brief.baima.adaptation: This chapter sets Baima and Yanjin as two battles back to back: Yan Liang dies of arrogance, Wen Chou of rashness. Beyond Yun Chang's blade, what truly bears reading is the temper of each man.
brief.baima.boss.loss: The first victory went to the second battle's head; Hebei keeps at least one of its twin walls, and the siege of Baima is not lifted.
brief.baima.boss.title: Baima and Yanjin · Two Generals Slain
brief.baima.boss.why: Yan Liang commands presence through linked camps and banners; Wen Chou pursues with iron cavalry and hot anger. Two battles in a row—you must win each one more calmly than the last.
brief.baima.boss.win: Both battles broken, both blades clean; Guan Yu trades his great merit for a passport to seek his brother, and the last paper screen between Cao and Liu is torn through.
brief.baima.lead: Yan Liang has cut down two generals in a row, and no one in Cao's camp dares answer. Cao Cao does not look at his officers—only at the man who keeps his back turned to every battle report. He knows that blade is waiting on word of a letter.
brief.baima.record: Yuan Shao sent Yan Liang to besiege Baima. Guan Yu spied Yan Liang's command canopy, thrust him down amid ten thousand soldiers, and rode back. Wen Chou arrived later at Yanjin; his army fell into disorder, and he died in the rout.
brief.baima.skirmish.loss: The vanguard is wiped out, and morale breaks first beneath the walls of Baima; even if Yun Chang rides out, he must first pay for the panic of the whole camp.
brief.baima.skirmish.title: Liyang · Cao's Vanguard
brief.baima.skirmish.why: Song Xian, eager to prove himself to his old lord, seized the front rank. You must protect that eagerness without letting a pointless sacrifice grind down Cao's will to fight again.
brief.baima.skirmish.win: The vanguard falls back but its lines hold; Cao's camp keeps its strength, and the hour for Yun Chang to ride out has come.
brief.baima.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Guan Yu, Annals of Emperor Wu · Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapter 25
brief.baimenlou.adaptation: This chapter puts Lü Bu and Chen Gong on the same enemy side: you must win not only Lü Bu's war chest but also make two stubborn men admit a way out.
brief.baimenlou.boss.loss: The rope still tightens on the White Gate Tower; Lü Bu and Chen Gong return to the record's ending. This chapter's main gate stands unchanged, and the old pages follow as before.
brief.baimenlou.boss.title: White Gate Tower · Cornered Beast and Strategist
brief.baimenlou.boss.why: Lü Bu fears that bowing his head means no longer being himself; Chen Gong fears one more victory means the whole city is buried with them. You must break both deadlocks at once.
brief.baimenlou.boss.win: Lü Bu is willing to ask where to retreat; Xiapi buys another way to live, and Cao Cao at Xudu will reckon you anew.
brief.baimenlou.lead: The fires of Wancheng have barely died when Cao Cao besieges Xiapi. The man from Hulao who only ever wanted to go forward has met a wall his halberd cannot pierce.
brief.baimenlou.record: Cao Cao besieged Xiapi; Lü Bu, hemmed in with Chen Gong and others at his side, came out and surrendered, and was finally strangled. Chen Gong was executed too. The White Gate Tower was no simple contest of courage.
brief.baimenlou.skirmish.loss: A charge with no direction exhausts the last strength of the defenders, and no matter how clever Chen Gong's plan, there are none left to carry it out.
brief.baimenlou.skirmish.title: Si River · Outpost of a Trapped City
brief.baimenlou.skirmish.why: The camp-breakers are still looking for a way through, while flood and hunger in the city worsen daily. Stop this reckless advance first, and then men will listen to Chen Gong.
brief.baimenlou.skirmish.win: The breakout is halted, and Lü Bu for now does not trade soldiers for another famous victory; you may bring one last plan up the White Gate Tower.
brief.baimenlou.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Lü Bu
brief.bossMeta: Decisive at the gate · win to rewrite the page
brief.bowang.adaptation: This chapter follows the Romance timeline and "the strategist's first use of fire," while the historical note openly flags the date gap. This isn't blending two records into one fact.
brief.bowang.boss.loss: The fire fails to close its ring, and Xiahou Dun breaks through the slope. The strategist's first credit in the original scroll is not earned on this map.
brief.bowang.boss.title: Bowang Slope · First Use of Fire
brief.bowang.boss.why: Xiahou Dun drives straight at you with elite troops, meaning to smash the ambush with speed. You must hold back from an early showdown and tighten both the fire route and his arrogance at once.
brief.bowang.boss.win: Bowang burns. The strategist's first order holds, and the generals begin taking commands by the whole picture, not by reputation. But urgent word from Changban is already close.
brief.bowang.lead: The Longzhong Plan gave the far road; Bowang Slope brings the near enemy first. The new strategist must make arrogant generals believe that a map can truly become a fire.
brief.bowang.record: In the histories, the battle of Bowang took place in the seventh year of Jian'an, when Liu Bei ambushed and defeated Xiahou Dun — before the three visits to Zhuge. The Romance recasts it as Zhuge Liang's first fire attack after leaving the cottage.
brief.bowang.skirmish.loss: The lure becomes genuine chaos, the ambush is scattered by the fleeing troops, and the strategist's first order loses its credit.
brief.bowang.skirmish.title: The Xinye Road · Luring the Enemy onto the Slope
brief.bowang.skirmish.why: Cao's vanguard presses close. You must make retreat look like a real rout, not an empty town recognized at a glance.
brief.bowang.skirmish.win: The vanguard is drawn onto the prepared road; ambush and fire route fall into place, and Xiahou Dun still thinks he's chasing a broken army.
brief.bowang.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of the First Sovereign · Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapter 39
brief.caochuan.adaptation: This chapter keeps the heavy fog, the drums, and the borrowed arrows, and writes the risk of not being able to see your opponent's cards as a match on the river. Cao Cao's suspicion is both the source of the arrows and the thing that turns on him.
brief.caochuan.boss.loss: There is no fog on the river, or the drums fall out of order, and the straw boats become targets. Both the three-day promise and the alliance's mutual trust take the blow.
brief.caochuan.boss.title: Cao's River Fort · Borrowing Arrows in the Fog
brief.caochuan.boss.why: In the fog Cao Cao will not come out lightly and will only test you with volleys of arrows. You must turn his caution into your supply rather than send the fleet into an encirclement.
brief.caochuan.boss.win: The fog lifts and the boats are full. Jiangdong has its arrows, and for the first time Cao Cao realizes others have been reading him as a hole card. The chained barges and the fire attack follow close behind.
brief.caochuan.lead: With an alliance now possible, supply needs and mutual suspicion come to the table together. Zhou Yu wants arrows, Cao Cao wants calm, and Zhuge Liang wants a night of fog in which no one can see clearly.
brief.caochuan.record: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, the allied Sun-Liu forces and Cao's army faced each other across the river. But Zhuge Liang borrowing arrows from Cao's camp with straw boats is not recorded in the main text of the Records of the Three Kingdoms and should be clearly treated as a famous passage of the Romance.
brief.caochuan.skirmish.loss: Before the boats leave port, suspicion spreads through your own camp. The three-day promise is left as a boast that cannot be kept.
brief.caochuan.skirmish.title: Xiakou · Borrowing Boats and Men
brief.caochuan.skirmish.why: The Jiangdong sailors obey only the rules of river warfare and will not hand over their boats to some strange scheme from nowhere. You must first prove this is not a hollow boast that gambles an entire crew.
brief.caochuan.skirmish.win: Boats, straw bundles, and drummers are all in place, and Lu Su is willing to sail along as witness. The fog-night borrowing of arrows now has conditions it can actually meet.
brief.caochuan.source: Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapter 46 · set against the historical events at Red Cliffs
brief.changban.adaptation: This chapter expresses the pressure of the pursuit through a three-man enemy formation, and keeps Changban's first clear-table rematch. The game isn't about heroes slaughtering every pursuer, but about buying time for the people and the child to escape.
brief.changban.boss.loss: Changban scatters men and horses both, and the road to Hanjin is sealed. If this was your first clear-table loss, you may wheel about and charge once more.
brief.changban.boss.title: Changban Slope · Before the Broken Bridge
brief.changban.boss.why: Cao Cao, Xiahou Dun, and Zhang He press from three sides. You must knock out the whole enemy formation to win Zhao Yun the time to search and Zhang Fei the last breath to hold the bridge.
brief.changban.boss.win: The pursuers are held at Changban, and the child and companions cross toward Hanjin. The spark that will become Red Cliffs is not extinguished here.
brief.changban.lead: One fire at Bowang won't stop Cao Cao's march south. Between Xinye and Hanjin, what matters most are the people who can't move fast — not another pretty victory.
brief.changban.record: Cao Cao marched south, and Liu Bei withdrew with the people, only to be caught at Changban. Zhao Yun shielded Lady Gan and the heir; Zhang Fei held the broken bridge by the water. The seven charges in and out are literary flourish.
brief.changban.revive.loss: The second charge is encircled again, and the scattering in the original scroll stands. This page returns to history; the Lesson will remember that a way out must be kept for people.
brief.changban.revive.title: Changban Slope · Wheeling About
brief.changban.revive.why: The first charge opened no gap, and the child in your arms and the people at your back remain. You cut your way out and then back in, only to bring home the names you left behind.
brief.changban.revive.win: One wheeling strike wins the moment to break the bridge. Changban is no longer just a rout, but an apocrypha where someone was willing to come back for the lost.
brief.changban.skirmish.loss: The column is cut apart, the child and the people scattered. Even with famed generals still standing, you've lost what this battle was meant to protect.
brief.changban.skirmish.title: Dangyang · Tiger and Leopard Cavalry in the Crowd
brief.changban.skirmish.why: The Tiger and Leopard Cavalry cut into the slow-moving column. You must open a gap between the people and the child, and keep the retreat from turning into a stampede.
brief.changban.skirmish.win: The pursuers are delayed; Zhao Yun and Zhang Fei each gain room to rescue, and the column keeps moving toward Hanjin.
brief.changban.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biographies of the First Sovereign, Zhang Fei, and Zhao Yun · Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapters 41–42
brief.chencang.adaptation: This chapter turns siegecraft into reading a man: what Hao Zhao defends is not a city but a single word—"trust." Beyond ladders and fire arrows, the real calculation is whose arrives first, his grain or Chang'an's relief troops.
brief.chencang.boss.loss: The ladders burn out and relief arrives; the failure of the assault becomes the most painful lesson of the second northern campaign.
brief.chencang.boss.title: Chencang · Ladders and Letters
brief.chencang.boss.why: Hao Zhao does not trade tempers with you; he races you on "who arrives first." Letters of surrender and siege ladders take turns; you must reckon clearly the race between cook smoke, the grain road, and the relief army.
brief.chencang.boss.win: Wang Shuang is killed, and the army withdraws whole; Hao Zhao holds the city, the Chancellor wins ease in Longyou—in this battle neither man lost.
brief.chencang.lead: Chencang is small as a game piece, yet the man who holds it makes a thousand do the work of ten thousand. By the time the twentieth rank of ladders burns, even Wei Yan has begun counting the days again.
brief.chencang.record: On Zhuge Liang's second campaign, he came out through Sanguan and besieged Chencang; Hao Zhao held with barely a thousand men, breaking in turn siege ladders, battering rams, tunnels, and inside agents. Liang withdrew when his grain ran out; the Wei general Wang Shuang pursued and was killed.
brief.chencang.skirmish.loss: The hammer cracks Sanguan open, and both the grain road and the relief route run free; every day of the siege credits the defenders.
brief.chencang.skirmish.title: Sanguan · Wang Shuang's Hammer
brief.chencang.skirmish.why: Wang Shuang's meteor hammer clears the way for the relief force; hold him off first, and the siege engines at Chencang can go up.
brief.chencang.skirmish.win: The fierce general is checked, the relief route delayed; the length of the siege now rests with the attackers.
brief.chencang.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Zhuge Liang and Biography of Cao Zhen with the account of Hao Zhao · Romance, Chapters 97–98
brief.chibi.adaptation: Cao Cao, Zhou Yu, and Zhuge Liang at one table is the Writer's metaphor for the card game, not a claim that the Sun-Liu allies were enemies at Red Cliffs. You must read all three schemes at once.
brief.chibi.boss.loss: Wind, fire ships, and hearts were not all in place at once. The old page of Red Cliffs is not rewritten, and Cao Cao's chained barges still press down on the river.
brief.chibi.boss.title: Red Cliffs · One Torch for the Chained Barges
brief.chibi.boss.why: Cao Cao wants to steady the chained ships, Zhou Yu wants to seize the moment the fire starts, and Zhuge Liang wants to wait until everything is in place. You must bring all three schemes to bear on the outcome at once.
brief.chibi.boss.win: The chained barges turn to ash, Cao Cao retreats north, and the three-way balance of power gains room to breathe. The beaten army is about to enter Huarong Road.
brief.chibi.lead: The arrows are borrowed and the boats are chained. What is truly hard to obtain is each side bearing the consequences on the same night. The wind is not a gift from the sky; it is a chance everyone waits for together.
brief.chibi.record: At Red Cliffs, Huang Gai feigned surrender and struck with fire ships; Cao's army was driven back by fire and sickness. Zhuge Liang ascending the altar to summon the east wind is a Romance invention, not the sole reason the allies won.
brief.chibi.skirmish.loss: The fire ships are intercepted far off, and both the feigned surrender and the wind lose their mark. The allies must face a long standoff again.
brief.chibi.skirmish.title: Three Rivers Mouth · The Fire Ships Open the Way
brief.chibi.skirmish.why: The northern river horsemen hold the channel. If the fire ships cannot get near the chained barges, even a perfect southeast wind only fills empty sails.
brief.chibi.skirmish.win: The river mouth is opened. Huang Gai's squadron gets its line of attack, and the fire attack turns from a plan in a tent into a blow that can be struck.
brief.chibi.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Annals of Emperor Wu, Biography of Zhou Yu · Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapters 47–49
brief.daodan.adaptation: This chapter turns the banquet into a card table: Lu Su stakes "trust," the ambushers wait for "the blade." Whoever rushes first loses first; as long as Guan Yu's blade stays sheathed, it is his greatest chip.
brief.daodan.boss.loss: The cup falls, the blade comes out, blood on the river; the alliance shatters on the spot, and Cao Cao laughs aloud on the northern bank.
brief.daodan.boss.title: Lukou · A Banquet on the River
brief.daodan.boss.why: Lu Su demands Jing Province's trust; Guan Yu guards a brother's honor. Keep both the loan note and the crescent blade where they are, and let only words cross the table.
brief.daodan.boss.win: The blade stays sheathed, the account unbroken; one cup of wine buys Jing Province several more years of peace.
brief.daodan.lead: The invitation was written three times, each more courteous than the last. Axemen sit ready in the cabin, yet the letter says only two words: old times.
brief.daodan.record: Lu Su invited Guan Yu to a single-blade meeting to discuss Jing Province; both sides had ambushes in place but neither sprang. The histories note that "single blade" meant every officer came with one blade; the Romance turns it into Guan Yu going alone, a feat of valor.
brief.daodan.skirmish.loss: The ambush hangs over your head like a blade; every word at the table comes out three parts softer.
brief.daodan.skirmish.title: Baqiu · Ding Feng's Ambush
brief.daodan.skirmish.why: Ding Feng hides short blades beneath the tables, looking first for a flaw in the banquet. Spot the ambush's position before he does, and your words at the feast will carry weight.
brief.daodan.skirmish.win: Every ambusher's position is known; the initiative at the feast is yours. Lu Su's arguments can only be made across the table.
brief.daodan.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Biography of Lu Su · Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapter 66
brief.dingjunshan.adaptation: Xiahou Yuan and Zhang He form two enemy arrays, one swift and one slow. You must use terrain and timing, not simply write Huang Zhong as a legend of the old general whose single blade never misses.
brief.dingjunshan.boss.loss: The swift and slow arrays rescue each other, and the stroke from the heights cuts only air; Hanzhong remains deadlocked, and the old general can only wait for another chance.
brief.dingjunshan.boss.title: Dingjun Mountain · Swift Edge and Late Strike
brief.dingjunshan.boss.why: Xiahou Yuan quells chaos with speed; Zhang He patches the gaps by coming late. You must throw their rhythms out of step and win Huang Zhong the one downward stroke from the heights.
brief.dingjunshan.boss.win: Xiahou Yuan falls and Zhang He can no longer mend the field; the gate to Hanzhong stands open. Next, Guan Yu will meet his greatest hour on the Mian River.
brief.dingjunshan.lead: Yi Province is settled, and Hanzhong becomes the next threshold. What the old general lacks is not a name for valor, but a chance to make everyone admit he can still decide the field.
brief.dingjunshan.record: At Dingjun Mountain, Liu Bei's army struck from the heights, and Huang Zhong, with Fa Zheng and others planning in concert, cut down Xiahou Yuan in battle—tilting the Hanzhong campaign from there.
brief.dingjunshan.skirmish.loss: Cao's army steadies itself on the strong ground, and the old general is forced to seek battle on an unfavorable slope; the chance is lost before the troops are.
brief.dingjunshan.skirmish.title: Yangping Pass · To Take the Heights, First Take the Ground
brief.dingjunshan.skirmish.why: Cao's troops hold the mountain mouths. Attack uphill along the old road, and even Huang Zhong's courage only spends soldiers at the foot of the slope.
brief.dingjunshan.skirmish.win: The pass defenders are drawn out of position, and the high ground Fa Zheng points to opens a corridor; the momentum at Dingjun Mountain begins to turn toward Liu Bei.
brief.dingjunshan.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biographies of the Former Lord, Huang Zhong, and Fa Zheng
brief.fengyiting.adaptation: This chapter adopts the Romance's characters and the setting of Fengyi Pavilion, seating Dong Zhuo and Lü Bu in suspicion at one table; the Writer cares more about whether Diao Chan can reclaim her own words.
brief.fengyiting.boss.loss: The chain of schemes is dismissed as cheap provocation, and the two join forces to drive you from the table first; Diao Chan remains trapped in someone else's answer.
brief.fengyiting.boss.title: Fengyi Pavilion · Father and Son at One Table
brief.fengyiting.boss.why: Dong Zhuo holds on through favors granted, Lü Bu repays through obedience. You must let the two men's suspicions press on each other—not choose a home for Diao Chan in their stead.
brief.fengyiting.boss.win: The bond between father and son splits open, and Dong Zhuo and Lü Bu can no longer share a table; Diao Chan walks out of Meiwu, and Lü Bu's path departs the record by a single step.
brief.fengyiting.lead: After Hulao, Lü Bu returns to Meiwu. A single halberd can break an enemy's position, but the crack in the bond between father and son cannot be pried open by brute force.
brief.fengyiting.record: In the third year of Chuping, Wang Yun and others conspired with Lü Bu to kill Dong Zhuo. The histories record no meeting at Fengyi Pavilion, nor any Diao Chan who maneuvered between them with a chain of schemes as in the Romance.
brief.fengyiting.skirmish.loss: The word is distorted before it ever reaches the pavilion, and the two will simply fix their suspicions on you; the scheme is exposed before the first hand is dealt.
brief.fengyiting.skirmish.title: Meiwu · Beyond the Beaded Curtain
brief.fengyiting.skirmish.why: Dong Manor's guards seal off every path of speech outside the pavilion; a single word misdelivered will turn the chain of schemes into nothing but jealous gossip before it begins.
brief.fengyiting.skirmish.win: The guards are drawn away, Dong Zhuo and Lü Bu can at last hear each other across one table, and Diao Chan keeps her own arrangements intact.
brief.fengyiting.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, 'Biography of Lü Bu' · Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapters Eight and Nine
brief.ganlu.adaptation: This chapter freezes that halberd in midair: beyond victory and defeat, this page wagers on the historian's next line. The Son of Heaven's only chip is his name—how not to stake it all at once is your question.
brief.ganlu.boss.loss: The Son of Heaven's blood splashes the palace bricks; Sima Zhao executes Cheng Ji to appease the realm. Blade and guilt go back into the sheath together.
brief.ganlu.boss.title: South Tower · The Halberd in Midair
brief.ganlu.boss.why: Jia Chong does not strike the blow himself—he only puts the blade in Cheng Ji's hand. You must cry down that order, which answers only to its master, and make the guards see the Son of Heaven—and see themselves.
brief.ganlu.boss.win: The halberd does not fall; the guards scatter. The historian dips his brush and writes straight: 'The emperor marched against the traitor.' Wei draws one more breath.
brief.ganlu.lead: On Lingyun Terrace, the twenty-year-old Son of Heaven finished 'Hidden Dragon' and snapped his brush. He summoned the last old ministers and gave them no decree—only one sentence: Sima Zhao's heart is known to every passerby.
brief.ganlu.record: In the fifth year of Ganlu, Cao Mao led several hundred palace guards and servants against Sima Zhao; Jia Chong ordered Cheng Ji to kill the emperor beneath the southern gate tower. Mao loved letters and once wrote the poem 'Hidden Dragon' in grief for himself.
brief.ganlu.skirmish.loss: The brush outruns the sword; the Duke of Jin's office hears first, and the march becomes a walk into the snare.
brief.ganlu.skirmish.title: Taiji Hall · The Informer's Brush
brief.ganlu.skirmish.why: Wang Shen's brush always leaves the palace first. Stop that brush, and the emperor's march may yet take them by surprise.
brief.ganlu.skirmish.win: The secret memorial never clears the palace gate; the guards at the south tower know nothing, and the emperor rides before them in person.
brief.ganlu.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Annals of the Three Young Emperors · Chronicles of Han and Jin · Romance, chapter 114
brief.gaopingling.adaptation: This chapter uses feigned illness as the opening puzzle, writing the edict, the armory, and the hearts of the people as the real pot. If Wuzhang Plains has already been changed, Zhuge Liang will send an old letter reminding you not to look only at old age.
brief.gaopingling.boss.loss: Cao Shuang yields power; the Sima clan takes control. The Gaopingling Incident unfolds in full as in the original record; his false tell will become the next Lesson.
brief.gaopingling.boss.title: Gaopingling · Beyond the Sickbed
brief.gaopingling.boss.why: Sima Yi trades frailty for Cao Shuang's complacency. You must expose the illness while guarding the transfer of power; unmasking the performance without holding the gate still loses.
brief.gaopingling.boss.win: The coup is intercepted. Cao Shuang does not lightly hand over the seals, and the old page of Sima supremacy is rewritten—though years later, Yinping will still have its dangerous road.
brief.gaopingling.lead: After Wuzhang Plains, the man who best understood waiting returns to Luoyang. The realm no longer watches only the Crouching Dragon and the Tomb Tiger; everyone who assumed he would simply fall ill and die has been counted into the hand.
brief.gaopingling.record: In the tenth year of Zhengshi, Cao Shuang accompanied the Wei sovereign Cao Fang to pay respects at Gaopingling. Sima Yi launched a coup in Luoyang, seizing the armory and the palace. Cao Shuang surrendered his power and was executed soon after; from then on, Wei's authority passed to the Sima clan.
brief.gaopingling.skirmish.loss: The household troops seize the key points first. The old man on the sickbed has not even risen, and Luoyang already has a new master.
brief.gaopingling.skirmish.title: Luoyang · Household Troops Stir in Secret
brief.gaopingling.skirmish.why: The Sima household troops use sick-visits and condolence calls to mask their movements. Stare only at the sickbed, and you will miss the real shifts at the armory and the palace gates.
brief.gaopingling.skirmish.win: The secret movements are pinned down in advance. The empress dowager's edict and the armory have guards; even with his eyes open, Sima Yi cannot simply collect the whole city.
brief.gaopingling.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biography of Cao Shuang; Book of Jin: Annals of Emperor Xuan
brief.guandu.adaptation: This chapter turns the disparity in troops and supply into Yuan Shao's swollen war chest and rising blinds. You can lean on Xu You and Wuchao, or you can win by breaking the enemy's will first.
brief.guandu.boss.loss: Cao's army breaks first for want of grain, and the pressure of the original scroll becomes your fate. The Lesson will note that you cannot play for attrition against him here.
brief.guandu.boss.title: Guandu · Night Fire at Wuchao
brief.guandu.boss.why: Yuan Shao means to outlast you with his deep war chest until you slip first. You must find the soft spot between his grain route and his men's hearts before the blinds climb out of reach.
brief.guandu.boss.win: Wuchao falls, and Yuan's great formation loosens from within. The old page of the north is rewritten — and in a thatched cottage soon, a plan for three will be spoken.
brief.guandu.lead: By the time Guan Yu went north, the two powers of the north were already locked at Guandu. What you stake next isn't a single pass or a single general, but the north for a decade to come.
brief.guandu.record: Cao Cao and Yuan Shao faced off at Guandu, the one short of men, the other short of grain. Xu You's defection and the burning of the grain at Wuchao turned the tide, and Yuan Shao's army collapsed. The shape of the north changed with it.
brief.guandu.skirmish.loss: The raiders shut off all word, and Cao's camp is left with shrinking grain ledgers. You bleed out before Yuan Shao even offers battle.
brief.guandu.skirmish.title: Baima and Yanjin · Outposts on the Grain Road
brief.guandu.skirmish.why: Screening cavalry from Hebei keep cutting the scouts and grain routes. If not even true tallies can reach Guandu, the fire at Wuchao will remain a tale told in tents.
brief.guandu.skirmish.win: Grain route and intelligence flow again. You can now tell Yuan's paper numbers from the men who can actually fight.
brief.guandu.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, Annals of Emperor Wu and Biography of Yuan Shao
brief.guijin.adaptation: This chapter uses Sima Yan as the poker-table embodiment of "unification"; it does not send him to lead troops at Jianye in person. You are to ask whether unity and the erasure of difference must be the same thing—while acknowledging the people's genuine need for peace.
brief.guijin.boss.loss: Sun Hao surrenders; the realm enters Jin as the record dictates. Peace does arrive, but you left no further words for those on the back of the surrender document.
brief.guijin.boss.title: Jianye · The Last Hand of All Under Heaven
brief.guijin.boss.why: Sima Yan's greatest card is ending the chaos. You must prove that peace is worth cherishing—but that it does not mean every name from the Three Kingdoms should be wiped away in a single stroke.
brief.guijin.boss.win: The tower ships pause; unity is no longer the only grammar. The old pages of the Three Kingdoms are fully read, and the Writer will lay open the final hand to you on the back of the paper.
brief.guijin.lead: After Yinping, only the last old banners remain. Wang Jun's tower ships sail east, and Jianye's surrender will soon be written. What you face is not another famous general, but the saying itself: after long division, all must unite.
brief.guijin.record: In the first year of Taikang, Wang Jun and other Jin commanders sailed down the river to Jianye, and Sun Hao surrendered; Wu fell. The division that had lasted nearly a hundred years since the Yellow Turban Rebellion was at last briefly reunified under Western Jin.
brief.guijin.skirmish.loss: The river and the city gate are lost together; beyond the surrender document, ordinary people's names are the first to be erased by war. When the realm is finally united, only the victor's version remains.
brief.guijin.skirmish.title: Stone City · Tower Ships at the Gates
brief.guijin.skirmish.why: The Jin vanguard holds the river and the city gates. What is first contested is not the three old banners, but whether the people and the grain markets can be spared plunder when the city falls.
brief.guijin.skirmish.win: The defenses and the people's livelihood are held for now. Jianye need not buy unity with slaughter; you earn the right to discuss with Sima Yan how to unite.
brief.guijin.source: Book of Jin: Annals of Emperor Wu; Records of the Three Kingdoms: Biographies of the Three Successor Rulers
brief.huainan.adaptation: This chapter joins the last two rebellions into two linked battles: Guanqiu Jian falls to grain and betrayal from within, Zhuge Dan to suspicion and waiting. Wen Yang's spear is Huainan's last gate—but a gate is not a city.
brief.huainan.boss.loss: The banners on Shouchun's walls change three times; Wu's relief is always one step late, and the Sima blade falls faster each time.
brief.huainan.boss.title: Shouchun · Two Rebellions Joined
brief.huainan.boss.why: Guanqiu Jian gathers men by righteousness; Zhuge Dan waits behind walls for relief. You must read how differently the two rebellions die—one short of grain, one full of suspicion—before you can speak of rewriting them.
brief.huainan.boss.win: The proclamation reaches Luoyang, and the word 'Wei' burns hot in soldiers' hearts again; Sima Shi's eye ailment and his realm ache together.
brief.huainan.lead: After Sima Yi's death, the first proclamation against the traitor rose in Huainan. Over the next four years the same fire burned this land three times; the names changed, the words did not.
brief.huainan.record: Three rebellions in Huainan—Wang Ling (251), Guanqiu Jian (255), Zhuge Dan (257–258)—all failed. Guanqiu Jian died in defeat; Zhuge Dan held Shouchun until the city fell and his clan was wiped out; Wen Yang drove back the pursuers single-handed.
brief.huainan.skirmish.loss: Bottled up in a lonely city, the proclamation cannot leave Shouchun; the two rebellions fight alone and are eaten one by one.
brief.huainan.skirmish.title: Huainan · Yue Chen's Defense
brief.huainan.skirmish.why: Yue Chen holds Huainan by the formations his father left behind. Break his gate first, or the proclamation never leaves the city.
brief.huainan.skirmish.win: The gate is open and the loyalist troops link east to Wu; the two rebellions can answer each other and live.
brief.huainan.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms, biographies of Guanqiu Jian and Zhuge Dan · Book of Jin · Romance, chapters 110–112
brief.huarong.adaptation: This chapter keeps both unofficial histories: the blade falls, or the blade does not. The card game only contends over whether Cao Cao reaches you. Whether you spare him out of old loyalty and what follows are still yours to choose.
brief.huarong.boss.loss: Cao Cao passes Huarong. You gain neither the kill that military order demanded nor the loyalty of letting him go by your own choice—only the escape of your target.
brief.huarong.boss.title: Huarong Road · Before the Blade Falls
brief.huarong.boss.why: Cao Cao pleads old debt for his life and argues the northern threat if he dies. Win his war chest first, and only then are you entitled to decide who bears the blade falling or not falling.
brief.huarong.boss.win: Cao Cao's fate is in your hands: the blade falling would change the north, the blade staying would preserve old loyalty. Both consequences will be written into the pages that follow.
brief.huarong.lead: The fire at Red Cliffs lit up Cao Cao's defeat and left you a question harder than victory or loss: old debt, military order, and the realm—which should the blade fall for in the end?
brief.huarong.record: It is recorded that after his defeat at Red Cliffs Cao Cao passed through the dangerous Huarong road, where the mud and the exhaustion of his soldiers were severe. That Guan Yu was ordered to guard it and let Cao go out of old loyalty is the Romance's most famous choice.
brief.huarong.skirmish.loss: The beaten soldiers re-form into a line, and Cao Cao slips away through the gap. The ambush at Huarong waits on an empty road.
brief.huarong.skirmish.title: Wulin · The Last Flame of a Beaten Army
brief.huarong.skirmish.why: The remnants of the defeated army fight to the death to hold their retreat. You must cut off their route before they re-form, not let the carnage drag you into a pointless pursuit.
brief.huarong.skirmish.win: The remnant guards are broken apart, and Cao Cao can only go toward Huarong. You are about to face a problem that cannot be solved with an all-in.
brief.huarong.source: Records of the Three Kingdoms: Annals of Emperor Wu, Pei Songzhi's note quoting the Records of the Duke of Shanyang · Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Chapter 50
brief.hulao.adaptation: Hulao and the Three Heroes' duel with Lü Bu follow the Romance. At the table, Lü Bu 'advances and never retreats,' turning the pressure of the world's finest into a betting rhythm you can read.
brief.hulao.boss.loss: Lü Bu still stands before the pass in invincible form, and the record remains unchanged; the Lesson will remind you not to mistake his fearsome name for your own fifth card.
brief.hulao.boss.title: Hulao Pass · Best Under Heaven
brief.hulao.boss.why: Lü Bu demands the lords acknowledge that none can match him; you must prove that valor has more than one way forward, and that it is not an unreadable decree of fate.
brief.hulao.boss.win: The halberd crashes to the ground, and the best under heaven remembers your name; the old pages of Xiapi and Fengyi Pavilion now hold new possibilities.
brief.hulao.lead: Hua Xiong has barely withdrawn, and before the lords can even squabble over the credit, the gates of Hulao have opened. The true best in the realm disdains to wait for your reputation.
brief.hulao.record: The allied army against Dong Zhuo and Dong Zhuo's forces stood locked in a standoff. Lü Bu was indeed famed for his ferocity, but the three heroes—Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei—fighting Lü Bu together is not recorded in the histories.
brief.hulao.skirmish.loss: One after another the lords' banners fall back, and Lü Bu need not even ride out from the pass; fear has already won a hand on his behalf.
brief.hulao.skirmish.title: The Hulao Road · Wolves Test Their Fangs
brief.hulao.skirmish.why: Bingzhou's wolf riders hunt before the pass, singling out any banner that shows fear first. You must steady the ranks before you earn the right to study Lü Bu's halberd.
brief.hulao.skirmish.win: The wolf riders fail to break the formation; the three heroes and you find your positions to sweep the field together, and the road before the gates of Hulao is cleared.
