story.huarong.intros.caocao.0.bio: From the plum wine to Red Cliffs, every time the road narrows he still remembers how to talk old friendship with you.
story.huarong.intros.caocao.0.quote: Plum wine. Fleet on fire. You and I meet again on a narrow road.
story.huarong.intros.caocao.1.bio: A beaten army cannot guard him, so he has pressed yesterday's kindness into service as his personal guard.
story.huarong.intros.caocao.1.quote: Today I speak not of the empire. Only of old acquaintance.
story.huarong.intros.guanyu.0.bio: From Hulao to Huarong, his given word has always weighed more than the blade — and been harder to set down.
story.huarong.intros.guanyu.0.quote: You have seen how Guan draws the blade. Today, watch why he sheathes it.
story.huarong.intros.guanyu.1.bio: The signed military order in his bosom, the old kindness in his heart — he will let no man sign either entry for him.
story.huarong.intros.guanyu.1.quote: Guan stands here. Neither loyalty nor honor may be borrowed in another's name.
story.huarong.loss.clue: Lesson · Cornered, Cao Cao will push the oath and the old kindness onto the table in turn. On retry, reading improves — and the final choice is still yours to make.
story.huarong.loss.text: Cao Cao walks out of the mud all the same. You were busy doing Guan Yu's arithmetic of loyalty for him — and forgot his oldest talent: making others win him his survival.
story.huarong.map.0.choices.0.detail: Cao's troops open with -1 morale; remember the oath signed
story.huarong.map.0.choices.0.text: Unroll the military order; read the articles of war first
story.huarong.map.0.choices.1.detail: Reading improves; remember the old kindness
story.huarong.map.0.choices.1.text: Fold the military order away; hear only the old debt
story.huarong.map.0.lines.0.text: If Yunchang kills me, he honors his oath. If he lets me go, he repays an old debt. Which entry will you have him answer for?
story.huarong.map.0.lines.1.text: He has framed his one road to live as two debts. Listen — which does it sound like?
story.huarong.map.0.lines.2.text: Neither. While the blade lives in a living hand, dead sentiment should not decide the day.
story.huarong.map.0.title: Huarong · Two Ledgers Under the Blade
story.huarong.objective: Win through to the end of his road, then choose with your own hand: let the old debt fall with the blade, or let honor become the debt Maicheng must one day repay.
story.huarong.win.hook: Whether or not the blade falls, word of it will travel through Jingzhou all the way to Maicheng. Winter is still far off. The entry is already made.
story.huarong.win.text: Cao Cao's last chips scatter into the mud, and the road is quiet enough to hear the ring of the blade. Guan Yu finally looks at you. Ahead, no one bars the way; behind, the oath still stands. Winning the hand has not written your ending — it leaves both the falling and the holding of that stroke in your hand alone.
story.hulao.battle.0.text: Your chips are like the lords' courage — they look plentiful enough.
story.hulao.battle.1.text: The better his run, the more he writes his strong hands on his brow. Don't do his frightening for him.
story.hulao.battle.2.text: Good! Now it deserves the name Hulao!
story.hulao.battle.3.text: So 'never retreat' was never courage — just the only way he knows how to win.
story.hulao.coldOpen.0.text: One lazy point of the painted halberd up on the pass, and the lords' banners seem to shrink a head shorter. You have only just arrived when Liu Bei slides a cup of wine in front of you.
story.hulao.coldOpen.1.text: My second brother's cup took Hua Xiong's head. This cup today — do you dare take it?
story.hulao.coldOpen.2.text: Everyone knows how this page ends. No one knows why you are in it.
story.hulao.coldOpen.3.text: You again. What we left unfinished last time — settle it all today.
story.hulao.intros.lvbu.0.bio: He remembers you across the table last time, and how you took down the pot.
story.hulao.intros.lvbu.0.quote: Don't wave the lords at me. You — come up alone.
story.hulao.intros.lvbu.1.bio: Before Hulao Pass, 'peerless under heaven' is the shortest challenge he knows how to write.
story.hulao.intros.lvbu.1.quote: All three heroes at once, or you alone. Don't keep me waiting.
story.hulao.loss.clue: Lesson · Lü Bu magnifies fear with relentless pressure; on restart, his false tells come fewer.
story.hulao.loss.text: You retreated with the lords. Only after leaving Hulao do you understand: all along he was forcing you to treat 'finest under heaven' as a fifth community card.
story.hulao.map.0.choices.0.detail: +100 war chest; Lü Bu starts with -1 morale
story.hulao.map.0.choices.0.text: Ask the Three Heroes to stand at your flank
story.hulao.map.0.choices.1.text: Watch him play out one hand alone
story.hulao.map.0.lines.0.text: His strength was never playing every hand — it is that once you flinch, he no longer needs cards at all.
story.hulao.map.0.lines.1.text: Why all this talk! Let me go tip him over a round for you first!
story.hulao.map.0.title: Sishui · The Three Heroes' Old Pact
story.hulao.objective: Read Lü Bu's advances and retreats, and win your first 'impossible' before Hulao Pass.
story.hulao.win.hook: Before he fled, Lü Bu learned your name. The next meeting will not be at Hulao.
story.hulao.win.text: The painted halberd hits the ground, and the lords make no cheer. Liu Bei steadies you first; Guan Yu picks up the cup that was never touched.
story.jiameng.battle.0.text: Ma Chao! Take my spear! If I do not drink you under the table today, old Zhang is no Zhang at all!
story.jiameng.battle.1.text: Two hundred torches turned the field to daylight. The two spears knotted and unknotted in the glare until the men on the terraces forgot to cheer.
story.jiameng.battle.2.text: Cousin, fall back! Zhang Lu's relief will never get here, and there is barely anyone of ours left!
story.jiameng.battle.3.text: ...Those two bowls at the edge of the field. Who are they for?
story.jiameng.battle.4.text: Yide, pull back three parts of your strength. This man is carrying something. However hot his spear burns, he has reached his limit.
story.jiameng.coldOpen.0.text: The beaten men of the southern Wei fled to Zhang Lu, and Ma Chao led his troops below Jiameng Pass. When Zhang Fei on the wall heard who had come, he laughed three times — then had his sworn pledge of abstinence pressed under the desk.
story.jiameng.coldOpen.1.text: Ma Chao! They say you chased Cao Cao so hard at Tong Pass he cut off his own beard? Good! Old Zhang likes nothing better than a strong man. Come on, three hundred bouts!
story.jiameng.coldOpen.2.text: Zhang Fei of Yan? Since Tong Pass they say the only man in the realm worth my spear is your little brother. Bring your horse over.
story.jiameng.coldOpen.3.text: Yide, this man's hatred makes him brave. You cannot take him by force. Remember one thing: fight him to the full, and do not kill him.
story.jiameng.coldOpen.4.text: Strategist, let Wenchang take a force around their rear. If General Zhang should falter—
story.jiameng.intros.machao.0.bio: He has never worked out whose ink that was at Weinan, and the grudge costs his spear three parts of its aim.
story.jiameng.intros.machao.0.quote: A divided camp wins nothing twice. This time it is only spear against spear.
story.jiameng.intros.machao.1.bio: Since that fight with Zhang Fei there is something in his spear he cannot name.
story.jiameng.intros.machao.1.quote: We meet again. This time we finish first, and talk after.
story.jiameng.intros.machao.2.bio: A general of a beaten army, staking the last of his dignity on one spear.
story.jiameng.intros.machao.2.quote: Xiliang is lost and I have no home left. This battle is all I have.
story.jiameng.intros.madai.0.bio: He guards his cousin's flank, and what is left of the Ma family.
story.jiameng.intros.madai.0.quote: My cousin's business is Ma Dai's business.
story.jiameng.intros.madai.1.bio: A silent swordsman of Xiliang; his blade is as heavy as what he carries in his chest.
story.jiameng.loss.clue: Lesson · This page is won and lost off the spearpoint. On a new run, let them go the full distance: counting the bouts wins the board, warming the wine wins the man.
story.jiameng.loss.text: In your hurry to hand Zhang Fei a win, you cut off what that spear was trying to say. Ma Chao reined in and rode back to his lines, and after that he shut his gate and would see no one.
story.jiameng.map.0.choices.0.detail: Tell reading up this round; remember the two hundred bouts
story.jiameng.map.0.choices.0.text: Count the bouts for Zhang Fei and husband his strength
story.jiameng.map.0.choices.1.detail: War chest +120; the two come to respect each other
story.jiameng.map.0.choices.1.text: Warm two bowls of wine and wait at the edge of the field
story.jiameng.map.0.lines.0.text: Dark ruins a good fight! You there, light the torches, two hundred of them! We fight by night!
story.jiameng.map.0.lines.1.text: Now that is spirit! Zhang Fei, you are more of a man than the stories said.
story.jiameng.map.0.lines.2.text: Torchlight shows the spear, and it shows the heart. Fight long enough and the spears do the talking.
story.jiameng.map.0.title: Jiameng Pass · A Night Fight by Torchlight
story.jiameng.objective: Beside the fire basin at Jiameng Pass, let the two fiercest spears under heaven fight their fight — then talk about who follows whom.
story.jiameng.win.hook: By the brazier at Jiameng, a Xiliang spear found a new direction. And in Jingzhou, Lu Su was inviting Yunchang across the river over a single borrowed note.
story.jiameng.win.text: After two hundred bouts the torches had burned half down. Zhang Fei planted his spear in the earth. 'Ma Chao, rest a night. We finish tomorrow!' Ma Chao sat his horse a long while without a word, then asked: 'General Zhang, can your lord Liu truly hold a grudge like mine in his house?' In the end three men shared those two bowls of warm wine: you, Yide, and a spear laid flat.
story.jiange.battle.0.text: Jiang Wei! Jiange may be steep, but your grain will run out before my brush does!
story.jiange.battle.1.text: This stretch of wall I have held for forty years without letting anyone through! Young man, push harder!
story.jiange.battle.2.text: Three posts at Yinping—all lanterns are lit! General, the front is safe—the wall is whole!
story.jiange.battle.3.text: Zhong Shiji, no matter how fine your manifesto, you cannot climb over this mountain. Go back and tell Sima Zhao: Shu still has men.
story.jiange.coldOpen.0.text: Eighteen thousand Wei troops pressed toward Jiange, and Jiang Wei held the pass by its cliffs. Zhong Hui's manifesto was elegantly written; a pity the Sword Gate only understood arrows.
story.jiange.coldOpen.1.text: Jiang Boyue, holding a lone city—do you hold it for loyalty, or for refusal to accept? Surrender the pass, and I will see you made a marquis.
story.jiange.coldOpen.2.text: Zhong Shiji's manifesto is prettier than your siege ladders. But the road to Jiange is one—your soldiers cannot spread out.
story.jiange.coldOpen.3.text: This old man has retreated from Maicheng all the way to Jiange, forty years of retreating. At this pass, Yuanjian retreats no more!
story.jiange.coldOpen.4.text: General, Zhang Yi has one more word: the Yinping trail must not go unguarded. If Deng Ai slips through, Jiange's cliffs will be an empty gate!
story.jiange.intros.zhonghui.0.bio: He memorized every banner before the pass; this time he added three more pages to his letter of surrender.
story.jiange.intros.zhonghui.0.quote: This time, I have even planned your way out of my surrender demand.
story.jiange.intros.zhonghui.1.bio: A noble son of Yingchuan: his brush is faster than his sword, and his ambition faster than both.
story.jiange.intros.zhonghui.1.quote: Taking Shu is like plucking a crown. Gentlemen, let us all pluck together.
story.jiange.loss.clue: Lesson · Zhong Hui presses 'momentum' against 'terrain,' alternating surrender demands and assaults. On replay, fix the wall before setting scouts; his manifesto is the cheapest siege ladder he has.
story.jiange.loss.text: Zhong Hui's feint drew away your scouts, and the front at the Sword Gate thinned to paper overnight. When the pass fell, Jiang Wei did not look back; he only raised his fists toward Yinping: 'Bogong, it is Wei who failed you.'
story.jiange.map.0.choices.0.detail: This replay: Tell detection up; remember wall-style defense
story.jiange.map.0.choices.0.text: Hold the front to the death; ignore the manifesto
story.jiange.map.0.choices.1.detail: Zhong Hui starts with -200 war chest; remember the flank's eye
story.jiange.map.0.choices.1.text: Split off three scouting posts to watch the Yinping road
story.jiange.map.0.lines.0.text: General, leave the front to me. But ugly words from Yi: Deng Ai is at Tazhong—if he does not take the main road—
story.jiange.map.0.lines.1.text: Rest easy, Bogong. I have scouts at Yinping and eyes at Jiangyou. Jiange guards not a door but an entire wall.
story.jiange.map.0.lines.2.text: No matter how thick the wall, someone must be willing to stand on it. These old bones will lean against it first.
story.jiange.map.0.lines.3.text: Zhong Hui only wants you to turn your head. Once you do, the front grows thin—let him shout, but do not let him pull you.
story.jiange.map.0.title: Jiange · The Pass and the Flank
story.jiange.objective: Hold Zhong Hui's great army at the natural fortress of Jiange—and shield Shu-Han from the word 'flank.'
story.jiange.win.hook: Jiange held the front, but on the snowline of Motian Ridge another lone army wrapped in felt was descending—that was the wind of the next page.
story.jiange.win.text: Zhong Hui besieged the pass for over twenty days; his grain ran out first, and his manifesto exhausted its last rhetoric. On the day he struck camp and withdrew west, he looked back at the Sword Gate and wrote Jiang Wei's name in his notes: 'Taking Shu is not hard; this man is the hard part.' And on the wall of Jiange, the old general Liao Hua fell asleep leaning on his long saber—for the first time in forty years, he slept before the pass.
story.jieqiao.battle.0.text: Shields — up! Crossbows — raise! Show the men of Youzhou what the Vanguard Corps is!
story.jieqiao.battle.1.text: Every time his shield drops, a crossbow rewinds. Count his rhythm, not his arrows.
story.jieqiao.battle.2.text: The white horses are broken! Hebei's spears — collect the debt!
story.jieqiao.battle.3.text: Half the volunteers are down... Zilong, you were right. Bogui rushed it.
story.jieqiao.coldOpen.0.text: The white-horse volunteers of Youzhou are called the finest cavalry under heaven — until, across the river at Jieqiao, eight hundred men of the Vanguard Corps quietly raise their crossbows.
story.jieqiao.coldOpen.1.text: One charge, and Hebei goes quiet for ten years. In Youzhou, Bogui has seen the strongest wolves — never wolves that know how to wait.
story.jieqiao.coldOpen.2.text: I came from Changshan to serve an army that holds its ground — not one that dies for nothing. General, their line is uneven. Something waits behind it.
story.jieqiao.coldOpen.3.text: Cavalry? Cross the river, and you're rows of targets that still breathe.
story.jieqiao.coldOpen.4.text: His Lordship says: today Hebei's spears teach Youzhou how they are used.
story.jieqiao.intros.quyi.0.bio: He remembers how your white horses swung wide of his crossbows last time; this time he keeps the shields lower still.
story.jieqiao.intros.quyi.0.quote: Swinging wide again? My crossbows have more than one row.
story.jieqiao.intros.quyi.1.bio: His eight hundred men have all seen blood, and not one of them fears a horse.
story.jieqiao.intros.quyi.1.quote: Come across the river. My crossbows have waited a long time.
story.jieqiao.intros.wenchou.0.bio: Yan Liang's name is his scar and his fire — he heard that battle was lost in a fog no one could explain.
story.jieqiao.intros.wenchou.0.quote: Of Hebei's twin walls, one is down. Today I make up the difference.
story.jieqiao.intros.wenchou.1.bio: He still disputes the last battle — but his spear has put away three parts of its contempt.
story.jieqiao.intros.wenchou.1.quote: This time I wait for you to cross first.
story.jieqiao.intros.wenchou.2.bio: He and Yan Liang are called the twin walls of Hebei; the one thing he has over Yan Liang is patience.
story.jieqiao.intros.wenchou.2.quote: I'm in no hurry. My spear is longer than yours. I can wait.
story.jieqiao.loss.clue: Lesson · Qu Yi's crossbows win by making you charge. On retry his false tells are reduced; don't push the volunteers in at the half-crossing.
story.jieqiao.loss.text: At the half-crossing the crossbows speak as one, and the white horses fall in rows into the river. Zhao Yun holds the rear and pulls Gongsun Zan clear, then looks back at you once, and says nothing.
story.jieqiao.map.0.choices.0.detail: Reading improves this chapter; remember the peril of the half-crossing
story.jieqiao.map.0.choices.0.text: Dismount the vanguard, lock shields, lead the horses across
story.jieqiao.map.0.choices.1.detail: War chest +100; Vanguard opens with -1 morale
story.jieqiao.map.0.choices.1.text: White horses at full gallop, straight into the Vanguard
story.jieqiao.map.0.lines.0.text: The bridge is narrow, the horses packed tight. If the Vanguard looses at our half-crossing, no number of white horses can form a line.
story.jieqiao.map.0.lines.1.text: Zilong is too careful. Once, with a few dozen riders, I cut clean through the Xianbei wolf packs.
story.jieqiao.map.0.lines.2.text: A breakthrough lives on surprise. The men across the river are waiting for exactly one thing — your charge.
story.jieqiao.map.0.title: Jieqiao · The Half-Crossing
story.jieqiao.objective: At Jieqiao, shield the White Horse Volunteers from the Vanguard Corps' crossbows — and win Zhao Yun his first duel the world actually sees.
story.jieqiao.win.hook: Gongsun Zan wins the field and loses to his own high walls. Meanwhile, at Fengyi Pavilion in Mei, another rift between father and son is waiting to bloom.
story.jieqiao.win.text: You count the crossbow line down to its last beat; the white horses wheel in three troops, and the shield wall finally cracks at one corner. When Wen Chiu spears in to save it, Zhao Yun's point holds him off: 'A steady spear, General — a pity it serves a proud man.' Yuan Shao's center falls back across the river. On both banks of Jieqiao, the name Zhao Zilong of Changshan is known from this day.
story.jieting.battle.0.text: Ma Su is on the hill? Then there is no need to rush a climb. First ask how many rounds his waterskins will last.
story.jieting.battle.1.text: Cutting the supply road is the feint. Testing the water line is the real move. Do not chase that banner waving back and forth.
story.jieting.battle.2.text: Pass the order: camp on the road. Wang Ping did not beat me. Jieting matters more than my winning.
story.jieting.battle.3.text: You are willing to come down off the hill, and half my odds go with it. So there is a man beside Zhuge Liang who will admit a mistake.
story.jieting.coldOpen.0.text: Chancellor, the classics put it plainly: place men on death ground and they live. From that hilltop I look down on all Jieting. However many Zhang He sends, I break that many.
story.jieting.coldOpen.1.text: Commander Ma, the classics mention water as well. That hill you circled is so high — have you seen how many days a soldier must walk down before he drinks?
story.jieting.coldOpen.2.text: Youchang, what I asked you to hold was not a handsome formation diagram. If no one dares contradict you today, then the fault starts with me.
story.jieting.coldOpen.3.text: The tidier the banners on that hill, the better. Then I need only ring the foot of it, and let him die of thirst on my behalf.
story.jieting.intros.zhanghe.0.bio: He has already waited out one hilltop's weakness at Jieting. This time he even knows where the water line will be cut.
story.jieting.intros.zhanghe.0.quote: Hill or water — which one will you leave to the enemy this time?
story.jieting.intros.zhanghe.1.bio: Zhang He does not contest you for a fine position. He only forces you to admit that beyond terrain there are also days, and thirst.
story.jieting.intros.zhanghe.1.quote: War has no fixed shape. You made the hill into one.
story.jieting.loss.clue: Annals · Zhang He feints at the supply road and truly seals the water. On replay he opens at -1 morale; guard the bottom of the pot before you look to strike back.
story.jieting.loss.text: The shouting broke on the hilltop first; the blades came after. What Zhuge Liang seemed to be condemning was not only Ma Su, but the man in himself who knew Ma Su loved to show off, and gave him Jieting anyway.
story.jieting.map.0.choices.0.detail: Zhang He opens at -1 morale; remember the joint defense
story.jieting.map.0.choices.0.text: Have Ma Su and Wang Ping co-sign the camp defense order
story.jieting.map.0.choices.1.detail: Read bonus this round; remember the water-source map
story.jieting.map.0.choices.1.text: Take Ma Su to walk the water route below the hill himself
story.jieting.map.0.lines.0.text: If I listen to Wang Ping today, will the whole army say I know war only from books — or will I finally admit there was a page I never understood?
story.jieting.map.0.lines.1.text: Commander, changing an order is no disgrace. Let the men live to see morning first; our pride can wait its turn.
story.jieting.map.0.title: Jieting · Water First, Then the Hill
story.jieting.objective: Get Ma Su to rewrite "high ground always wins" into the road and the water source — hold Jieting before Zhang He arrives, and hold his life with it.
story.jieting.win.hook: Jieting held, and Sima Yi turned toward Xicheng instead. No Ma Su waited there — only a qin and an open gate.
story.jieting.win.text: By the time Zhang He arrived, the road camp had already bitten into the pass mouth, and the water details were shuttling safely through the back ravine. Ma Su struck the hilltop fort off the map with his own hand. Zhuge Liang did not weep; he only had him sit down beside Wang Ping and rewrite that order.
story.kongcheng.battle.0.text: An empty city makes you a bluff. A city full of ambush makes you a trap. I need only decide which mistake costs less.
story.kongcheng.battle.1.text: Do not watch his hand. Watch how every raise makes him fear the consequence a little more. The empty city sells him his own caution.
story.kongcheng.battle.2.text: What he fears is not the ambush. It is that if he strikes wrong, the world will say he lost to an empty city.
story.kongcheng.battle.3.text: If a string snaps, I go in. If it holds, I must think longer. Kongming, you would spend even a broken string to deceive me.
story.kongcheng.coldOpen.0.text: The hinges of Xicheng had been oiled, and would not give even a creak. The old and the weak swept the streets below; on the wall stood a single qin.
story.kongcheng.coldOpen.1.text: The fire at Bowang, the wind at Red Cliffs — I have replayed them both. Kongming, what have you prepared for me today?
story.kongcheng.coldOpen.2.text: Jieting did not fall, and still he bites down on Xicheng. So he did not come for Ma Su. He came to make me admit to his face that I have no troops.
story.kongcheng.coldOpen.3.text: The defeat report from Jieting is in my sleeve, and the old and the weak are below the gate. Zhongda wants to see my weakness — then give him the one that looks most true.
story.kongcheng.intros.simayi.0.bio: He retreated once at Xicheng. Every note of a qin since has sounded like a reminder of the day he could not bear to lose.
story.kongcheng.intros.simayi.0.quote: The same city. I will not retreat for you a second time.
story.kongcheng.intros.simayi.1.bio: Jieting did not drain the Shu army for him, so he has come himself to read Zhuge Liang's riskiest stroke.
story.kongcheng.intros.simayi.1.quote: Ma Su did not break, so you think I cannot see through Xicheng as well?
story.kongcheng.intros.simayi.2.bio: He remembers your bets, and he remembers letting a whole city go because he had calculated one layer too deep.
story.kongcheng.intros.simayi.2.quote: This time, shall I think one layer less, or one layer more?
story.kongcheng.intros.simayi.3.bio: For the first time the Tomb Tiger sits across from the Crouching Dragon. His sharpest weapon is not troops; it is being willing to think one layer deeper.
story.kongcheng.intros.simayi.3.quote: If no one is in that city, why do you dare invite me in?
story.kongcheng.loss.clue: Annals · Sima Yi weighs the price of your bluff, not merely its boldness. On replay, fewer false tells — do not run the same betting line twice.
story.kongcheng.loss.text: The Wei troops were already through the gate while the qin still held its last note. Sima Yi did not smile. He only said: "You wagered that I fear being wrong. This time I will pay the price of being wrong."
story.kongcheng.map.0.choices.0.detail: Sima Yi opens at -1 morale; remember the slow qin
story.kongcheng.map.0.choices.0.text: Play the last pass of the qin even slower
story.kongcheng.map.0.choices.1.detail: Sima Yi -200 supplies; remember the dust decoy
story.kongcheng.map.0.choices.1.text: Raise dust in Xie Valley to fake reinforcements
story.kongcheng.map.0.lines.0.text: If he enters, I lose. If he retreats because he cannot bear to lose, we win. Wipe the gate cleaner still — leave nothing that looks like a cover-up.
story.kongcheng.map.0.lines.1.text: And if this time he would rather be wrong, and come in to look?
story.kongcheng.map.0.lines.2.text: Then the qin cannot merely sound calm. It must let him hear that I have already counted his refusal to admit error among the ambushers.
story.kongcheng.map.0.title: The Wall Tower · Who Is the Qin Played For
story.kongcheng.objective: Turn having no troops into a price Sima Yi dares not pay — let the qin, the gate, and his own suspicion each hold a line.
story.kongcheng.win.hook: The empty city cost each of them a breath; Wuzhang Plains will settle the account. This time Sima Yi has decided not even to listen to the qin.
story.kongcheng.win.text: The qin fell away to the foot of the wall, and at last Sima Yi reined in. Thirty li out he looked back at the empty gate: "I did not lose to an ambush. I lost to not daring to lose." Zhuge Liang's palms were soaked, but he only told the boy to light another brazier of incense.
story.luofengpo.battle.0.text: Pang Tong — for a man who truly reads fortune and peril, you never should have entered this slope.
story.luofengpo.battle.1.text: Listen: every arrow chasing Dilu. Zhang Ren guards 'Liu Bei must ride the white horse' — not Luofeng Slope.
story.luofengpo.battle.2.text: The phoenix banner swings east, the ambush swings east. What they call the falling phoenix — I can choose where it lands.
story.luofengpo.battle.3.text: The white horse false, the banner false. You took my own caution and bent it into your bow.
story.luofengpo.battle.4.text: Shiyuan — the ambush is in disarray. Today we trade no horses. We trade for a road they never wrote down.
story.luofengpo.coldOpen.0.text: Before Luofeng Slope, Dilu refuses the white stone path. Pang Tong dismounts, presses the reins back into Liu Bei's hand — and suddenly asks whether Zhang Ren means to kill the horse, or the man.
story.luofengpo.coldOpen.1.text: Kongming's letter said only: peril heavy, fortune light, for general and commander alike. He plotted me into that count — and forgot the ambush must recognize a face before it shoots.
story.luofengpo.coldOpen.2.text: The roads of Shu your father and brother held for thirty years, and now someone truly breaks in... Rener — the gates of Chengdu are in your hands.
story.luofengpo.coldOpen.3.text: Shiyuan, trading horses was a kindness. What if that kindness wrote your death register for you?
story.luofengpo.coldOpen.4.text: No arrows until you see Dilu. I want Liu Bei. Kill the wrong man and it is all for nothing.
story.luofengpo.intros.zhangren.0.bio: He remembers the ambush springing on empty air; this time he questions every banner more closely.
story.luofengpo.intros.zhangren.0.quote: Banners can be swapped. The heart that guards this land, you cannot swap.
story.luofengpo.intros.zhangren.1.bio: First in loyalty and valor in the Western Rivers; his caution is his city wall — and his ambush's signal.
story.luofengpo.intros.zhangren.1.quote: Until the white horse appears, no man looses an arrow without orders.
story.luofengpo.loss.clue: Lesson · Zhang Ren confirms the banner before he gives the order; before the volley, there is one moment of misrecognition. On retry, reading improves.
story.luofengpo.loss.text: You were careful to leave Dilu behind, then rode on along the mountain path Zhang Ren had already chosen. You dodged the recognized horse, not the calculated man — and the second volley of arrows waits for no signal.
story.luofengpo.map.0.choices.0.detail: Spot the ambush; remember the white-horse decoy
story.luofengpo.map.0.choices.0.text: Lead Dilu riderless at the head of the column
story.luofengpo.map.0.choices.1.detail: Ambush opens with -200 war chest; remember the false banner
story.luofengpo.map.0.choices.1.text: Swing the arrow storm wide with a phoenix-plume banner
story.luofengpo.map.0.lines.0.text: Deep woods, a fast horse. But my ambush waits on one signal only: the white horse enters the slope, ten thousand arrows fly.
story.luofengpo.map.0.lines.1.text: He means to shoot the fixed idea that Liu Bei must ride Dilu. A place's name need not defeat me — but a horse's name deceives men.
story.luofengpo.map.0.lines.2.text: Then let that fixed idea lead the way for us — one last time.
story.luofengpo.map.0.title: Luofeng Slope · Turning the Ambush's Own Eye
story.luofengpo.objective: Use Dilu and Zhang Ren's fixation on the Young Phoenix to make the ambush loose its arrows at the wrong target.
story.luofengpo.win.hook: With the Young Phoenix in Shu, Hanzhong becomes the next card no one can leave unclaimed. On Dingjun Mountain, Huang Zhong is polishing a blade that refuses to grow old.
story.luofengpo.win.text: The arrow storm falls on an empty horse and a false banner, and Pang Tong climbs the high ground by the side slope. He takes no relief in a hex broken; he only adds four characters to the letter that read 'peril heavy, fortune light': And so with men's hearts. For the first time, a crack shows in Chengdu's gates — wide enough for the Young Phoenix.
story.maicheng.battle.0.text: Lu Xun let you believe there was still time. I am here to see it run out. Yunchang — time to see things differently.
story.maicheng.battle.1.text: Every time you asked for aid, I thought it through for the man receiving the letter first. By the time you see it, the road is already my formation.
story.maicheng.battle.2.text: That mercy at Huarong was not so Cao Cao could live my death today. Lord Guan's honor has never charged interest in the north.
story.maicheng.battle.3.text: The blade fell at Huarong, and Lord Guan never regretted it. Only today do I understand: killing one man does not kill the world's calculations.
story.maicheng.battle.4.text: You gave Gongjin ten more years, but you never made Jiangdong forget Jingzhou. He owes you a life; I cannot repay him a city.
story.maicheng.battle.5.text: Splitting the letters isn't waiting for rescue — it's making Wu guess which road to block. Before any answer arrives, the decoys are already out the gate.
story.maicheng.battle.6.text: The old letters are ash; Lü Meng can only guess at today's Guan Yu. To break out, first make the old self disappear.
story.maicheng.battle.7.text: The beacons still burn. In the moment Lü Meng glances back at the wall, the small road under the snow is no longer the page he'd plotted.
story.maicheng.coldOpen.0.text: Snow covered the beacon towers of Maicheng. Lü Meng's white robes and Lu Xun's ribbon of office entered the tent, one after the other. On Guan Yu's desk lay a severed sword-tassel — left at Huarong, all those years ago.
story.maicheng.coldOpen.1.text: That day the blade did not fall, and Cao's armies stand idle in the north today. The mercy Lord Guan granted — it seems — comes back along the map to collect.
story.maicheng.coldOpen.2.text: That day the blade did fall, and the northern lords, each with private calculations, let his plea for aid die on the road at Linju. The debt of honor was cleared; the road did not widen.
story.maicheng.coldOpen.3.text: Father, I've scouted the way. The north path can be walked — but the woods around Linju are thick. I fear the Wu men have nets there.
story.maicheng.coldOpen.4.text: These legs outrun their horses! Mount up, my lord — I'll carry the blade and clear the road. Whoever blocks us, I trample!
story.maicheng.coldOpen.5.text: Yunchang, at your height you drowned seven armies. But allies and old enemies alike learned from that flood how to fight you.
story.maicheng.intros.luxun.0.bio: Gongjin lived because of you; Lu Xun means to prove that a saved life changes nothing about Jingzhou.
story.maicheng.intros.luxun.0.quote: You saved Gongjin. Jingzhou is another matter.
story.maicheng.intros.luxun.1.bio: The lower he bends his humility, the slower and tighter the nets close around Maicheng.
story.maicheng.intros.luxun.1.quote: The novice Lu Xun comes to learn from the man whose name shakes the empire.
story.maicheng.intros.lvmeng.0.bio: He knows you once let Cao Cao go home north — and he has counted that old mercy into your road of appeals.
story.maicheng.intros.lvmeng.0.quote: You could release the tiger. Can you walk the road my mercy left open?
story.maicheng.intros.lvmeng.1.bio: He remembers the blade falling at Huarong, and no longer hopes old kindness will slow your sword.
story.maicheng.intros.lvmeng.1.quote: You've already killed Cao Cao once — then you know I hold no old debt to repay.
story.maicheng.intros.lvmeng.2.bio: Beneath the white robes is no merchant — it's a man who has read Guan Yu too many times.
story.maicheng.intros.lvmeng.2.quote: Three days apart, and a scholar deserves new eyes. Yunchang — do you still recognize Lü Meng?
story.maicheng.intros.panzhang.0.bio: What he covets was never just the city. It's the eighty-two-pound blade inside it.
story.maicheng.intros.panzhang.0.quote: The Green Dragon Blade... time it found a new master.
story.maicheng.intros.panzhang.1.bio: The net-layerer's first calculation is not troop counts — it's the habits of a cornered man.
story.maicheng.intros.panzhang.1.quote: Men on the road in a snowstorm always pick the shortest way.
story.maicheng.loss.clue: Historian's note · Lü Meng and Lu Xun will work old debts and retreat routes against you in turn. On a rerun, upgrade your Read; your Huarong choice still yields different counsel.
story.maicheng.loss.text: Lü Meng played your old honor; Lu Xun played your new resolve. One sealed the road of appeals, the other waited out your hesitation. When the snow stopped, Maicheng remembered only the Guan Yu who refused to change.
story.maicheng.map.0.choices.0.detail: Supplies +150; Lü Meng +100; note the split letters
story.maicheng.map.0.choices.0.text: Split the appeals for aid north and west
story.maicheng.map.0.choices.1.detail: Read gains upgraded; note the burned letters
story.maicheng.map.0.choices.1.text: Burn the old letters; break out with picked men only
story.maicheng.map.0.choices.2.detail: Wu army opens with -200 supplies; note the empty beacons
story.maicheng.map.0.choices.2.text: Rekindle the beacons; pretend the hold still stands
story.maicheng.map.0.lines.0.text: We need not guess whether Guan Yu will surrender. Work out only whom he still trusts, and Maicheng has no second gate.
story.maicheng.map.0.lines.1.text: Jingzhou was not lost to a city or a general. It was lost because every man took his former self as today's signpost.
story.maicheng.map.0.lines.2.text: If the Huarong blade never fell, Cao Cao owes you a life. But his armies stand idle — repaying a debt, or waiting for Wu and Shu to bleed each other?
story.maicheng.map.0.lines.3.text: If the blade fell, the north has troubles of its own. You burned one road of rescue — and burned the enemy's old read of you with it.
story.maicheng.map.0.title: Linju · Old Debts, Snowbound Road
story.maicheng.objective: Unravel the snare of white robes and humble words woven around the man you used to be — so Guan Yu does not let an old debt from Huarong decide the road out of Maicheng.
story.maicheng.win.hook: Jingzhou held — but the name of vengeance does not fade so easily. The campfires of Yiling and the deathbed charge at Baidicheng both wait in the next volume, for you to rewrite.
story.maicheng.win.text: The west gate of Maicheng opened before the snow stopped, and Guan Yu led the survivors out through Linju. That stroke at Huarong — whether it fell or was withheld — opened no gate today. He left the old sword-tassel in the snow, and the living no longer trade old debts against new lives. Jingzhou still has a road back, and Shu-Han still has a hand to play.
story.nanjun.battle.0.text: Master Zhou! How's the wound? My drum beats louder today!
story.nanjun.battle.1.text: He beats his drum at me; I enter his rage in my ledger. Wait for the third watch to change—
story.nanjun.battle.2.text: The bells ring at Yiling! Cao Hong has divided his men — Jiangling's wall just grew thinner!
story.nanjun.battle.3.text: The commander has gone pale. I'll hold your line — win this one, then rest!
story.nanjun.coldOpen.0.text: The fires of Red Cliffs had barely gone out; Nanjun's flag still flew in Cao Ren's hands. Zhou Yu stood at the river in full armor, the arrow wound not yet closed, while Cao Ren set out a taunting drum on the wall.
story.nanjun.coldOpen.1.text: Cao Zixiao has held walls for ten years without tiring. To take Nanjun, you must first beat the heart of a man who will not come out.
story.nanjun.coldOpen.2.text: Is the commander's wound still open? This drum of mine beats for you alone. Lose your temper, and the gate will open — for you.
story.nanjun.coldOpen.3.text: Commander, leave Yiling to Xingba. Wherever the bells ring, that is Wu another step forward.
story.nanjun.coldOpen.4.text: Gongjin, I'll hold the line with you. An arrow wound fears no arrow — it fears anger.
story.nanjun.intros.caohong.0.bio: He holds the Yiling road for his cousin, on one article of faith: the lord's line of retreat must outlive his own.
story.nanjun.intros.caohong.0.quote: This pass bears the name Cao. Want through? Leave a toll.
story.nanjun.intros.caoren.0.bio: He remembers how you shielded Zhou Yu from his own rage. This time he can't even be bothered to beat the drum.
story.nanjun.intros.caoren.0.quote: Again? This time I'll spare myself the theatrics.
story.nanjun.intros.caoren.1.bio: He has turned defense into a craft: no temper, no gambles, no grieving over a single brick.
story.nanjun.intros.caoren.1.quote: Every brick of Jiangling, counted. Come.
story.nanjun.loss.clue: Historian's note · Cao Ren's drum is a shackle for your temper. On a rerun his false tells shrink. Count his watch changes, not his insults.
story.nanjun.loss.text: At the third drum, Zhou Yu took up his spear and mounted, and the arrow wound split open along the seam of his armor. In the moment you caught him, Jiangling's gate burst open — that was exactly what Cao Ren had waited for.
story.nanjun.map.0.choices.0.detail: Read gains upgraded this round; note the rotation gap
story.nanjun.map.0.choices.0.text: Log the drumbeats and the relief rotations on the parapet
story.nanjun.map.0.choices.1.detail: Cao army opens with -200 supplies; note the split
story.nanjun.map.0.choices.1.text: Feint at Yiling to split his strength
story.nanjun.map.0.lines.0.text: Every day he beats that drum to mock my wound and goad me into pitched battle. If I fight, the wound tears. If I don't, morale rots.
story.nanjun.map.0.lines.1.text: Commander — record every drum he beats for you as a day he came out of the city.
story.nanjun.map.0.lines.2.text: The drum is his clock, not yours. Let it count his watch changes for you.
story.nanjun.map.0.title: Jiangling · The Drum Below the Wall
story.nanjun.objective: Match reads with Cao Ren beneath the walls of Jiangling, and spare Zhou Yu's arrow wound a second time splitting open.
story.nanjun.win.hook: Nanjong taken — and the ledger of Jingzhou turns its first page. In the north, hoofbeats are already grinding toward Tong Pass, riding on a load of hatred.
story.nanjun.win.text: The night Cao Ren abandoned the city and fled west, Zhou Yu climbed the wall of Jiangling pressing a hand to his wound. He accepted no cheers. He had the drum that had mocked him brought up, struck it three times with his own hand, and sent it back to Cao Ren: 'Thank it for me. It kept my patience.' Nanjun, at last, bore the name Sun.
story.qianli.battle.0.text: Dongling Pass honors the Chancellor's seal, not your old name. No papers — then the Green Dragon blade stays too.
story.qianli.battle.1.text: General Guan, Han Fu honors your name, but duty holds the gate. Once this arrow flies — forgive me.
story.qianli.battle.2.text: The wine at Zhenguo Temple is warmed. Leave the blade before the Buddha, and Bian Xi will show you a road to safety.
story.qianli.battle.3.text: The Xingyang guesthouse is clean, and the night is long. Why not rest, General — while I shut every door in the place for you?
story.qianli.battle.4.text: Here is the Yellow River. The goodwill of four passes is spent; Qin Qi answers only to General Xiahou's order.
story.qianli.battle.5.text: Five passes, five locks — but not every heart is a lock. When killing can be walked around, don't make it a sixth grave.
story.qianli.battle.6.text: Second Brother, hear the drums? No more guarding passes for anyone — come back and strike this one with me!
story.qianli.coldOpen.0.text: The gates of Xuchang behind him: the seal hangs high, the gold untouched. Guan Yu carries only the carriages and a blade that will owe no more favors.
story.qianli.coldOpen.1.text: That day over wine, Xuande hid his edge behind the thunder. Today Yunchang rides to find him. Should I let him go — or keep him for one more round of drinks?
story.qianli.coldOpen.2.text: I keep the Chancellor's kindness in my heart, but my oath to my brother waits on the road ahead.
story.qianli.coldOpen.3.text: Yunchang — these words in place of my face. Grieve for me no more than you would blame me. Come if you can. Someone in Gucheng is waiting.
story.qianli.intros.bianxi.0.bio: The incense of Zhenguo Temple cannot smother the smell of blood; his road to safety leads only to ambush.
story.qianli.intros.bianxi.0.quote: Leave the blade before the Buddha, drink the wine, and the General may sleep in peace.
story.qianli.intros.hanfu.0.bio: He keeps his respect hidden behind a bowstring, wanting one last piece of the old goodwill before he lets the arrow fly.
story.qianli.intros.hanfu.0.quote: General Guan, Han Fu honors you — but he cannot abandon his gate. After this arrow, bear me no grudge.
story.qianli.intros.kongxiu.0.bio: The lock at Dongling Pass recognizes only documents; he guards his duty more narrowly than his own life.
story.qianli.intros.kongxiu.0.quote: Without the Chancellor's pass, not even Guan Yunchang goes through.
story.qianli.intros.qinqi.0.bio: The last military order stands at the Yellow River ferry; he bars old acquaintances and rough water alike from the shore.
story.qianli.intros.qinqi.0.quote: Four passes behind you — so what? The Yellow River knows one flag only: Qin Qi's.
story.qianli.intros.wangzhi.0.bio: The guesthouse at Xingyang is too neat; every door has already decided when it will be locked.
story.qianli.intros.wangzhi.0.quote: The night is long and the road far. Why not stay — until the fire rises... until dawn, I mean?
story.qianli.loss.clue: Lesson · Kong Xiu spends your permits, Han Fu fires cold arrows, Bian Xi lays a feast, Wang Zhi reaches for fire, Qin Qi holds the ferry. Five passes share one life; don't bet the whole road fund on a single gate. On retry, war chest +150.
story.qianli.loss.text: You won the blade-light at some pass or other — and left the carriages, the chips, and the promised day behind you. The hardest part of the thousand li was never cutting a straight road through. It was arriving at Gucheng still entitled to say, 'Everyone is safe.'
story.qianli.map.0.choices.0.detail: Reading improves this chapter; remember the hearts along the road
story.qianli.map.0.choices.0.text: Trade rations for the common folk's telling of the five passes
story.qianli.map.0.choices.1.detail: Gate commanders open with -1 morale; remember the promise of the rear guard
story.qianli.map.0.choices.1.text: Take the rear guard yourself; send the carriages ahead
story.qianli.map.0.lines.0.text: Kong Xiu demands papers, Han Fu hides a cold arrow, and Bian Xi sets his wine before the Buddha. Different passes, different reasons to bar the road.
story.qianli.map.0.lines.1.text: No urging from the carriages. Guan Yu looks back down the road, then shifts his blade from right hand to left — only to put the drivers at ease.
story.qianli.map.0.title: Luoyang · Two Passes, One Bright, One Dark
story.qianli.objective: Escort the carriage train through five passes; learn how Kong Xiu, Han Fu, Bian Xi, Wang Zhi, and Qin Qi each mean to bar the way — and save your last strength for the reunion at Gucheng.
story.qianli.win.hook: The drums of Gucheng have not gone quiet; Yuan and Cao are deadlocked in the north. Next comes no lone ride through five passes, but two armies fighting for one breath of pride.
story.qianli.win.text: When Qin Qi falls, the roar of the Yellow River drowns the blade. Guan Yu does not count the fifth head; he turns and steadies the carriages. At the gate of Gucheng, Zhang Fei drops his drumsticks and seizes the horse in a hug. When Liu Bei arrives, Guan Yu says only, 'I'm late.' Three pairs of eyes give the same answer: late is fine. You came back.
story.qiqin.battle.0.text: You think one game bends my neck? The mountains of Nanzhong say no!
story.qiqin.battle.1.text: Last time it was a trip-line, not skill. Take me again if you dare!
story.qiqin.battle.2.text: I lost to my own carelessness, not to you. Next time I bring the rattan armor, the poison springs, and old friends.
story.qiqin.battle.3.text: You burned rattan armor, not the hearts of Nanzhong. I still do not yield!
story.qiqin.battle.4.text: Why release me every time you take me? Do you want me to yield to you, or to your Han law?
story.qiqin.battle.5.text: If I go home and raise troops again, it will look as though Nanzhong knows nothing but blades. Sit. Let us finish this hand.
story.qiqin.battle.6.text: You need not release me again. If I lose today, I acknowledge you for Nanzhong. If I win, you stay and drink a bowl with me.
story.qiqin.battle.7.text: Every time he rages, he asks why one more time. Do not stop up his questions. That is the only door Goading has.
story.qiqin.battle.8.text: You won the pot. I have not lost Nanzhong. Again!
story.qiqin.battle.9.text: If I turn on you now, the first thing I betray is the road home six times over.
story.qiqin.coldOpen.0.text: The miasma still hangs over the Lu River and the first trip-line is already strung. Zhuge Liang has ordered Meng Huo's wine bowl washed along with everything else.
story.qiqin.coldOpen.1.text: Bring as many men as you like; I will lend you as many mountains. Nanzhong is not a blank space on your map!
story.qiqin.coldOpen.2.text: If all I wanted was your surrender, one capture would do. What I want is for you to go home and no longer need a rebellion to prove who you are.
story.qiqin.intros.menghuo.0.bio: Nanzhong has already yielded in its heart, yet he will come back to the Lu River to see whether that yielding was an accident.
story.qiqin.intros.menghuo.0.quote: Yielding once does not mean I let you win seven more!
story.qiqin.intros.menghuo.1.bio: He remembers the seven rounds you never finished taking, and every place you set him down.
story.qiqin.intros.menghuo.1.quote: Last time we stopped early. The King of the South keeps his word. From the top!
story.qiqin.intros.menghuo.2.bio: He has the hardness of his mountains, the straightness of his wine, and one word, 'yield,' that he would sooner die than say first.
story.qiqin.intros.menghuo.2.quote: Beat me first, then talk to me about Goading!
story.qiqin.loss.clue: Lesson · Seven straight battles drain the pot. Leave yourself a way back before you take the man. On a new run the war chest starts at +150: do not shove the stack for one moment's satisfaction.
story.qiqin.loss.text: Meng Huo walked out of the camp gate again, and this time he did not look back. Not because he would not yield, but because you remembered only that he must be released six times, and forgot that each release owed him one more thing understood.
story.qiqin.map.0.choices.0.detail: Tell reading up this round; remember the pact of Nanzhong
story.qiqin.map.0.choices.0.text: Hear the Nanzhong elders out on the old customs
story.qiqin.map.0.choices.1.text: Share out grain and salt, send the prisoners home
story.qiqin.map.0.lines.0.text: You Han take a king and either kill him or cage him. If you truly let me go, are you not afraid I will come back with more men?
story.qiqin.map.0.lines.1.text: I am. That is why I do more than release you. I mean your people to see plainly, when you go back, who holds the salt and grain, who holds the mountain roads, who holds tomorrow.
story.qiqin.map.0.title: The Lu River · Let Him Go, Take His Heart
story.qiqin.objective: Seven battles are not only about taking the man. Bring Meng Huo from rage to suspicion to self-knowledge, until he says for himself what Nanzhong's tomorrow will be.
story.qiqin.win.hook: Nanzhong settled, the lamps burned in Hanzhong. Zhuge Liang unrolled the Memorial on the Campaign, and Qishan waited on the back of the page for a new road.
story.qiqin.win.text: The seventh time, Meng Huo did not wait for the soldiers to untie him. He set his crown on the table himself. 'Prime Minister, seven times is not my shame. It is seven times you believed I could still be reasoned with.' He turned and raised a hand to his people, and for the first time the drums of Nanzhong did not beat for war.
story.qishan.battle.0.text: Six campaigns out of Qishan? If you can come six times, I can hold six times. How many six-year spans can Ji-Han afford?
story.qishan.battle.1.text: He thinks endurance means standing still. Wrong. Endurance is keeping grain and men moving forward, day after day.
story.qishan.battle.2.text: I rode in and out seven times at Changban, and not so that later ages would recall me for a single word: brave. Today, watch how I come back.
story.qishan.battle.3.text: No fire, no surprise raid — and you still turned one camp at a time into an offensive?
story.qishan.coldOpen.0.text: That day at Longzhong I said the realm could be divided. Now the First Lord has handed me everything he could not finish, and I understand that threefold division is not an answer. Only a place to begin bleeding less.
story.qishan.coldOpen.1.text: However often that thatched door opened, I owe the men outside it that many answers. Today I march not to prove the Sleeping Dragon clever, but to stop writing 'another day.'
story.qishan.coldOpen.2.text: Prime Minister, Zhao Zilong of Changshan can still ask for the first scaling party. Do not write me off as an old banner for men to look back at, just because my hair has gone white.
story.qishan.coldOpen.3.text: Zhuge Liang, you write the affairs of state into a memorial; I write Qishan into a wall. Let us see whose words trap him first.
story.qishan.intros.caozhen.0.bio: Qishan was crossed once. He no longer merely holds the passes; he means to find that rejoined grain road and close it again.
story.qishan.intros.caozhen.0.quote: The same mountain road will not carry you twice.
story.qishan.intros.caozhen.1.bio: What he holds is not Qishan. It is Wei's old method: rest, wait, and drain Ji-Han dry.
story.qishan.intros.caozhen.1.quote: Write the finest memorial you like. Grain carts still will not cross the mountain by themselves.
story.qishan.loss.clue: Annals · Cao Zhen uses Qishan to wear down your patience. On replay, fewer false tells — learn to tell when he truly holds and when he is only waiting for you to push in.
story.qishan.loss.text: The wind flipped the Petition on the March back onto the desk. You did not lose to that wall named Cao Zhen. You treated the northern campaign as an all-in that had to be won at once, and forgot the mountain road had to be left standing for next year.
story.qishan.map.0.choices.0.detail: Cao Zhen starts at -1 morale; remember the feint from Changshan
story.qishan.map.0.choices.0.text: Send Zilong at Xie Valley with the old banners as a feint
story.qishan.map.0.choices.1.detail: War chest +200; remember the Qishan supply road
story.qishan.map.0.choices.1.text: Build the grain stations before you speak of advancing
story.qishan.map.0.lines.0.text: Cao Zhen has every one of my banners drawn in his ledger, and too many white hairs on my head. He thinks an old general is only good for a feint.
story.qishan.map.0.lines.1.text: When I first used fire at Bowang, the generals asked only when I would burn again. Today I will not. What Qishan needs is a road still walkable next year.
story.qishan.map.0.title: Qishan · A March Without Fire
story.qishan.objective: Turn the Memorial from a last testament into a beginning: at Qishan, open a northern road that grain and hearts can both travel for years.
story.qishan.win.hook: The road was open. The next gate was called Jieting. Ma Su had already spread the map across his tent table, and he had circled the hilltop hard.
story.qishan.win.text: The Qishan pass never broke, but the mountain road came alive first: supply post after supply post, and Zhao Yun's old banner folding back out of Xie Valley unharmed. Only then did Cao Zhen understand. Zhuge Liang had not wanted one entry through the gate; he wanted to be able to come again, every year after.
story.ruxu.battle.0.text: The river is too quiet. Pass the word to all camps: any alarm tonight — hold first, move second. Don't fall for feints!
story.ruxu.battle.1.text: The bells — RING! Brothers, let Cao's camp trample itself!
story.ruxu.battle.2.text: Fires at three points, and the drums of four hundred thousand tents beat against each other. Not one arrow knew where to fly.
story.ruxu.battle.3.text: The bells have stopped... count them — how many came back? One, two... all of them. Good. All of them is good.
story.ruxu.coldOpen.0.text: Cao Cao's four hundred thousand bore down on Ruxu, and Sun Quan's tent was dead silent. Gan Ning set a hundred bronze bells on the table, one by one, in a line.
story.ruxu.coldOpen.1.text: Mengde has Zhang Liao; I have Xingba. But a hundred riders into a camp of four hundred thousand — Xingba, I want you back alive.
story.ruxu.coldOpen.2.text: Rest easy, my lord. Bells ring, we ride; bells stop, we return. Xingba leads no hundred men to die — he leads a hundred men to collect a debt!
story.ruxu.coldOpen.3.text: Gan Ning! Always stealing the vanguard! My father's old troops are not all dead yet!
story.ruxu.coldOpen.4.text: Commandant, hold your tongue. Among this hundred ride old brothers of your own father.
story.ruxu.intros.caocao.0.bio: The fog of the straw boats and tonight's bells — Jiangdong's nerve has been entered in his ledger afresh.
story.ruxu.intros.caocao.0.quote: Borrowed my arrows, and now my camp. What gall!
story.ruxu.intros.caocao.1.bio: He remembers you borrowing his suspicion every time. Tonight he has simply spread that suspicion across four hundred thousand tents.
story.ruxu.intros.caocao.1.quote: Tonight, whoever touches my camp dies — the question is, who's doing the touching?
story.ruxu.intros.caocao.2.bio: The campfires of four hundred thousand turned the river white as noon — and magnified every shadow into an enemy.
story.ruxu.intros.caocao.2.quote: River rats, good only for fog and fire. In open battle, I'll wait for them.
story.ruxu.intros.lejin.0.bio: His name means 'advance', and so does the man — his vanguard is always one step ahead of the order.
story.ruxu.intros.lejin.0.quote: Vanguard camp, first over the wall! Men of Jiangdong — taste Yue Jin's blade!
story.ruxu.intros.xuhuang.0.bio: His formations live by one word — order. Even raiders get herded back the way they came.
story.ruxu.intros.xuhuang.0.quote: Raiding my camp? Pass these neat rows of stakes first.
story.ruxu.loss.clue: Historian's note · The hundred-rider raid wins by blinding eyes and ears, not by crossing blades. On a rerun: silence first, then the burst. Cao Cao's suspicion is your only ally inside.
story.ruxu.loss.text: The bells rang too early, and four hundred thousand woke out of their panic. The bells that came back numbered seventy. Gan Ning folded the string of thirty missing bells into his robe, and never spoke of that night again.
story.ruxu.map.0.choices.0.detail: Read gains upgraded this round; note the silence
story.ruxu.map.0.choices.0.text: Muffle the bells, hold silence — then explode
story.ruxu.map.0.choices.1.detail: Cao army opens with -200 supplies; note the fire signals
story.ruxu.map.0.choices.1.text: Raise fires at three points; let them spook themselves
story.ruxu.map.0.lines.0.text: One white goose feather each, held in the teeth. Inside the camp: kill no one. Cut banners, set fires, beat their own drums.
story.ruxu.map.0.lines.1.text: Youping holds the fort gate. At the second ringing of the bells, however many come back — the gate opens.
story.ruxu.map.0.lines.2.text: What a camp of four hundred thousand fears is not a hundred riders. It's not knowing how many riders came.
story.ruxu.map.0.title: Crossing the River · When the Bell Rings
story.ruxu.objective: Guard every ring of the hundred-rider night raid, and let Cao Cao's four-hundred-thousand-man army spend one night defeating itself.
story.ruxu.win.hook: The bells of Ruxu made the name of Hefei burn hotter. Zhang Liao waits there — to write the character 'Wu' into the nightmares of Jiangdong's sons.
story.ruxu.win.text: At dawn the count: a hundred riders, men and bells, not one missing. Cao Cao looked over a camp that had trampled itself for a night and told his staff: 'If Sun Quan's army is ordered like this, I cannot rush him.' He marched home. Sun Quan poured Gan Ning's wine with his own hand: 'Mengde has Zhang Liao; I have Xingba. That is enough.'
story.sangu.battle.0.text: First visit: the Master is away. You may win this hand, but you cannot win his consent to meet.
story.sangu.battle.1.text: Lost is lost, Brother. We come back tomorrow. Better than standing here guarding another man's door!
story.sangu.battle.2.text: Second visit: snow to the eaves of the thatched hall. You have come again — this time, do you seek a win, or do you seek a man?
story.sangu.battle.3.text: Yunchang, Yide — the snow is heavier; stand closer. The Master may decline to see us, but we must not lose the reason we came.
story.sangu.battle.4.text: The boy at the door and the cold welcomes of the first two visits — Liang borrowed both to ask you this: does victory make you swagger, and does defeat still bring you back? You came three times. The door should open.
story.sangu.battle.5.text: No talk of cards yet, General. Do you want Jing and Yi — or a world where the people no longer have to run?
story.sangu.battle.6.text: If the Master will not come down from the mountain, Bei will keep coming. If he walks with us, then this road belongs to more than Bei alone.
story.sangu.coldOpen.0.text: The road from Xinye to Longzhong — Liu Bei has walked it twice. Zhang Fei calls the third trip, through wind and snow, a waste of shoe leather. Guan Yu merely brushes off his brother's visiting card one more time.
story.sangu.coldOpen.1.text: Second Brother rode a thousand li and back, and now I get it — distance ain't the problem. But what kind of man makes us knock three times?
story.sangu.coldOpen.2.text: If he will come out of seclusion for the people, what is a few more walks to Bei?
story.sangu.coldOpen.3.text: Battles can be hurried; a door cannot. Yide, put the fire-striker away.
story.sangu.intros.zhuge.0.bio: Since Bowang he watches not only whether you have patience, but whether you can let another man take the credit.
story.sangu.intros.zhuge.0.quote: Since the thatched hall, you have learned to yield. Today — will you still wait?
story.sangu.intros.zhuge.1.bio: He remembers who won and lost on both earlier visits; he simply refuses to use either as a key to the door.
story.sangu.intros.zhuge.1.quote: I saw the wins and losses. Today — why have you come again?
story.sangu.intros.zhuge.2.bio: He listened to two snowstorms from behind the door; only on the third did he lay the world out on the table.
story.sangu.intros.zhuge.2.quote: Come in, General. Never mind the world for now — can you sit still long enough?
story.sangu.loss.clue: Lesson · Lose the first two visits and still return; don't stretch to win every hand. Save your strength for the third knock. On retry, war chest +150.
story.sangu.loss.text: On the third visit you finally see the map of Longzhong — and go right back to re-fighting the last two hands. Zhuge Liang folds his fan and says nothing. Patience is not walking a road twice more; it is hearing another man finish, even after you have seen the answer.
story.sangu.map.0.choices.0.detail: Sleeping Dragon opens with -1 morale; remember the courtesy of disarmed men
story.sangu.map.0.choices.0.text: Order the whole escort out of armor; wait quietly at the gate
story.sangu.map.0.choices.1.detail: Reading improves this chapter; remember the question that did not press
story.sangu.map.0.choices.1.text: Ask not about the world — ask first whether the Master sleeps well
story.sangu.map.0.lines.0.text: If he is out again today, I will leave my card. Seeking worthies does not mean the whole world must rise at Liu Bei's hour.
story.sangu.map.0.lines.1.text: Then I'll wait out here! And if waiting frays my temper, I'll count snowflakes — not his faults.
story.sangu.map.0.lines.2.text: If you can wait like that, Brother, this trip was already worth the cold.
story.sangu.map.0.title: Longzhong · A Door That Cannot Be Hurried
story.sangu.objective: Give each of the three knocks its own meaning: return after the first two visits whatever the score — and on the third, finally hear what the Sleeping Dragon truly wants to ask about the world.
story.sangu.win.hook: The plan of Longzhong is set — and Cao Cao's vanguard has reached Xinye. The Sleeping Dragon's first fire must first win over the two men who believe in it least.
story.sangu.win.text: Zhuge Liang writes Jing and Yi side by side under the same lamp, but writes nothing of host and guest. Liu Bei rises and bows low; Guan Yu sheathes his blade; Zhang Fei drags over a fourth stool for you. At last — a hand where nobody has to be made to concede.
story.sanqi.battle.0.text: You again, with another of Kongming's letters. Out with it — which city this time, and which line of 'Why was Yu ever born?'
story.sanqi.battle.1.text: Watch the hand where he folds good cards. He is not conceding — he is forcing himself to admit there is a next hand.
story.sanqi.battle.2.text: He waits for your mockery, so call only the cards. When no one catches his anger, the fire has nowhere to go but back into himself.
story.sanqi.battle.3.text: Why won't you laugh? If even my anger finds no landing place, am I not just another snapped string on your qin?
story.sanqi.battle.4.text: The third provocation need not be a sentence. Let him discover that losing can also fail to become a joke.
story.sanqi.coldOpen.0.text: The medicine at Baqiu has boiled black, but Zhou Yu presses the third letter of challenge under his qin. The first two angers drained his blood; the third, somehow, makes him laugh first.
story.sanqi.coldOpen.1.text: At Red Cliffs, one table — you made the wind your fuse. What will you use today to touch off my wound?
story.sanqi.coldOpen.2.text: Kongming's letter holds four characters: Why go this far? Gongjin reads it, then writes your name three times.
story.sanqi.coldOpen.3.text: If all you want is to beat him, one more jab suffices. If you want him to live, first give him one moment where he does not lose his composure.
story.sanqi.intros.zhouyu.0.bio: The fire of Red Cliffs beat Cao Cao — and lit up the pride that cannot stand behind any man.
story.sanqi.intros.zhouyu.0.quote: On the river you held the same instant. Here at Baqiu — will you wait for me to break first?
story.sanqi.intros.zhouyu.1.bio: His arrow wound unhealed, he hears every hesitation as a false note in his own music.
story.sanqi.intros.zhouyu.1.quote: The third letter? Read it. Let's see how many angers I have left.
story.sanqi.loss.clue: Lesson · Zhou Yu waits for your mockery before he strikes back. Catch less of his anger. On retry, reading improves.
story.sanqi.loss.text: You treated his loss of composure as the only winning door; the third jab landed, and with it every hand after this one closed forever. The qin did not break. The listeners left first.
story.sanqi.map.0.choices.0.detail: Reading improves; remember the third answer
story.sanqi.map.0.choices.0.text: At the letter's end, write out his line to victory
story.sanqi.map.0.choices.1.detail: Zhou Yu opens with -1 morale; remember: no goading
story.sanqi.map.0.choices.1.text: Have Lu Su carry away every goading word
story.sanqi.map.0.lines.0.text: He is certain every step you take is a laugh at him. Send medicine — he looks for poison; withdraw troops — he looks for ambush.
story.sanqi.map.0.lines.1.text: So the third letter offers no defense at all. It only sets down that hand at Red Cliffs — how he could have beaten me.
story.sanqi.map.0.lines.2.text: Handing your rival the winning line is harder than handing him the blame.
story.sanqi.map.0.title: Chaisang · The Third Letter
story.sanqi.objective: No more killing with a third provocation — let Zhou Yu, in his most wretched hand, see a road of his own to live.
story.sanqi.win.hook: Zhou Lang leaves Baqiu for a while — and the mountain roads into Shu are closing around Pang Tong. Luofeng Slope: Zhuge Liang stares at that name a long time.
story.sanqi.win.text: Zhou Yu does not cry 'Why was Yu ever born' again. He lays the letter — the one spelling out his own winning line — on the qin, plays one deliberate wrong note, and then, slowly, laughs at himself. Only when Lu Su hears the laugh does he dare let the physicians in.
story.shangfanggu.battle.0.text: Grain carts move north, ramparts lean east. Kongming, every step of yours invites me into the valley.
story.shangfanggu.battle.1.text: Father! The grain carts are in chaos—the Shu army truly is beaten! To chase or not—it must be now!
story.shangfanggu.battle.2.text: The valley gate—down! Fire arrows, up! Today the Wei army learns what it means to get in and not get out!
story.shangfanggu.battle.3.text: Trapped… Must we three, father and sons, end our lives in this valley? Enough—enough!
story.shangfanggu.coldOpen.0.text: South of the Wei, the Shu army farms its fields while the Wei army builds its ramparts. The mouth of Gourd Valley lies heaped with dry brush—waiting only for Sima Yi to walk in himself.
story.shangfanggu.coldOpen.1.text: Kongming farms his fields to invite me to a decisive battle; I will not oblige. If he retreats, I pursue—but only as far as the valley mouth.
story.shangfanggu.coldOpen.2.text: Father, the Shu grain carts have been moving north to the plain for days. Let me take a force and probe their strength.
story.shangfanggu.coldOpen.3.text: Sima Yi is not unwilling to come—he is unwilling to come alone. Then give his son a reason he cannot refuse.
story.shangfanggu.coldOpen.4.text: Chancellor, thirty wooden-ox grain carts are ready, and every one is marked—Weigong guarantees not a single cart will truly be lost.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simayi.0.bio: Since the lute at Xicheng, he trusts all the more that 'Kongming's retreats are always ambushes.' That suspicion is exactly the lock you need.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simayi.0.quote: I have heard that lute once. This time, I trust only my eyes.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simayi.1.bio: He still rests with eyes closed, yet hears in all directions—every mark you make at the valley mouth, he wants to know.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simayi.1.quote: Move your grain carts one more li forward. I am watching.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simayi.2.bio: The grave tiger does not leave his den—unless someone outside moves the stone from the entrance for him.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simayi.2.quote: Kongming, oh Kongming—your patience will lose to age in the end.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simazhao.0.bio: He has learned your ambushes before; this time he folds half his father's caution and adds it to his own resolve.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simazhao.0.quot: I learn half my father's caution. The other half, I rewrite.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simazhao.1.bio: The second son with the army, yet his eyes always rest on the chair in the command tent not yet warmed.
story.shangfanggu.intros.simazhao.1.quot: Junior General Sima Zhao, inspecting the valley on my father's behalf.
story.shangfanggu.loss.clue: Lesson · Sima Yi will probe again and again before he enters the valley. On a fresh run, read the clouds before you set the fire; the bait of abandoned grain cuts his war chest by 200—don't let the weather show its cards first.
story.shangfanggu.loss.text: The rain beat your fire by half a moment. Father and son in the valley laughed out loud in the downpour, and their laughter scalded hotter than the flames. At last you understood: the man who has accounted for every human thing, losing to Heaven's timing—nothing hurts worse.
story.shangfanggu.map.0.choices.0.detail: Insight increases this run; remember the choice of timing
story.shangfanggu.map.0.choices.0.text: Watch the cloud-line first, then fire on a dry day
story.shangfanggu.map.0.choices.1.detail: Wei army starts with 200 less war chest; remember the grain-cart bait
story.shangfanggu.map.0.choices.1.text: Sacrifice thirty grain carts, feign defeat into the valley
story.shangfanggu.map.0.lines.0.text: Chancellor, the task of luring the enemy should fall to Wen Chang! If Sima Yi will enter the valley, Wen Chang will take five hundred men and shut the gate behind him!
story.shangfanggu.map.0.lines.1.text: Wen Chang guards the valley gate—I am at ease. Only remember: once the fire starts, the gate must close fast—and open even faster.
story.shangfanggu.map.0.lines.2.text: Grain carts, dry brush, fire oil—the accounts are here. Chancellor, Weigong offers one reminder: the sky has gone three months without rain.
story.shangfanggu.map.0.lines.3.text: A rainless sky is fire's friend—and the prelude to rain. This round must be won faster than the weather.
story.shangfanggu.map.0.title: North Plain · The Grain-Cart Bait
story.shangfanggu.objective: Lure Sima Yi and his sons into Gourd Valley, and before the rain falls, let fire speak the Shu army's last word.
story.shangfanggu.win.hook: The fire in Shangfang Valley did not burn the Sima clan to nothing—but it burned away their arrogance. The autumn wind on the Wei riverbank is about to close out this standoff.
story.shangfanggu.win.text: By the time the fire took, the hand at the mouth of the valley was already played out. Sima Yi tilted his head back to the sky; the black clouds were pressing down from behind the mountain—but this time the rain fell after the burning was done. They pulled him up out of the ashes, and for a long moment he said only one thing: "Heaven's will abides; human works exhaust themselves first." From then on, the Wei army at Weinan never came out from behind its ramparts again.
story.shenting.battle.0.text: Little Conqueror — take my spear! Don't let anyone look down on the likes of us!
story.shenting.battle.1.text: Fine halberd work! Faster with the spear — the hand of a Sun does not shake yet!
story.shenting.battle.2.text: I've got your helmet — the armor's next. Still want more? I'll go all the way!
story.shenting.battle.3.text: When two tigers fight, one is bound to bleed — and the one who bleeds must hold a city tomorrow.
story.shenting.coldOpen.0.text: Outside Qu'a, scouts report: Sun Ce has taken twelve riders to probe Liu Yao's camp. Taishi Ci takes up his spear and mounts — followed by a single foot soldier who knows how to beat a drum.
story.shenting.coldOpen.1.text: They all call me the Little Conqueror. Today there's no line and no drum on this ridge — a fine time to see what's left under the title.
story.shenting.coldOpen.2.text: Taishi Ci of Donglai — a man who can't always feed himself, yet never loses with the spear. A fight, then. Let's see who blinks!
story.shenting.coldOpen.3.text: Bofu, the wind on Shenting Ridge is wrong. Midway through this fight, a third party will come.
story.shenting.intros.taishici.0.bio: That business with the halberd and the armor taught him your name — and your fairness.
story.shenting.intros.taishici.0.quote: You again. This time, lend me your eyes — let's see who deserves to win.
story.shenting.intros.taishici.1.bio: He has heard of the scroll-reader at Jieqiao who counted the drumbeats of a crossbow line; his spear carries three extra parts of respect.
story.shenting.intros.taishici.1.quote: A man who can count a crossbow line can surely count my spear.
story.shenting.intros.taishici.2.bio: He honors only two things in this life: his mother's teaching, and opponents worth beating.
story.shenting.intros.taishici.2.quote: The wind on the ridge is strong. Grip your weapon tight!
story.shenting.loss.clue: Lesson · This page asks not for a quick win, but for both men to fight the full match. On retry, watch who tires first before you bet.
story.shenting.loss.text: Your interference sours the duel, and both weapons point at you at once. Taishi Ci draws his spear back, disappointed: 'So even a scroll-reader can flip the table.'
story.shenting.map.0.choices.0.detail: Reading improves this chapter; remember the spear lines of Shenting
story.shenting.map.0.choices.0.text: Keep your hands folded; memorize both men's spear lines
story.shenting.map.0.choices.1.detail: War chest +120; both men fight all the harder
story.shenting.map.0.choices.1.text: Set wine on the ridge; wager on who tires first
story.shenting.map.0.lines.0.text: No orders here, no formation maps. Scheme for either man, and this fight is no longer clean.
story.shenting.map.0.lines.1.text: Good! Then clear the field. Gongjin, back off thirty paces — today is a duel. Anyone who interferes answers to me!
story.shenting.map.0.lines.2.text: Then I'll stand to one side and watch. Watch who shows his true skill first — and who shows his true self first.
story.shenting.map.0.title: Shenting Ridge · A Duel Without Drums
story.shenting.objective: On Shenting Ridge, let the two weapons fight to the very end of the match — leave Sun Ce and Taishi Ci both their dignity.
story.shenting.win.hook: The laughter on Shenting has not faded, and the map of Jiangdong waits to be drawn. In Xiaopei, a painted halberd is about to make peace between two houses.
story.shenting.win.text: The halberd snaps, the armor splits, and the two of them lie on the ridge hugging their weapons, gasping — then burst out laughing at the same instant. Taishi Ci sits up: 'Sun Lang, tomorrow on the field I won't yield an inch.' Sun Ce tosses him the broken halberd: 'Keep it. Mend it, and come again.' You pour the ridge-top wine into two bowls — one for the winner, one for the man who didn't lose.
story.shezhan.battle.0.text: We three will question you in turn. Stumble once, sir, and there is nothing more to discuss.
story.shezhan.battle.1.text: Cao Cao's strength is written in the histories. Will you buy your own renown with my lord's life?
story.shezhan.battle.2.text: No dodging. Governor Liu beaten again and again — is it not fact?
story.shezhan.battle.3.text: The House of Han is falling; it needs men who read the times. You won't even face the question of legitimacy — and you speak of restoration?
story.shezhan.battle.4.text: So Jiangdong must not gamble — because you fear your own names written on the page that resisted Cao.
story.shezhan.battle.5.text: Not one of them will write the word surrender alone, yet together they dare write it for a million people. Zibu — whose Jiangdong is this?
story.shezhan.coldOpen.0.text: Four desks stand in the council hall, three of them heaped with classics. Yours alone carries a single feather fan. Zhang Zhao opens by asking how many times Liu Bei has lost; Yu Fan already has the words 'a man without a home' waiting on his lips.
story.shezhan.coldOpen.1.text: Lord Cao commands a million men. With what will you resist him, sir? Do not mistake one dialogue at Longzhong for a talisman.
story.shezhan.coldOpen.2.text: Sir — what I want to hear is not whose classics are better thumbed, but who dares to carry Jiangdong's tomorrow.
story.shezhan.coldOpen.3.text: At Longzhong they asked you about the world; today they ask about winning and losing. Don't answer the wrong question.
story.shezhan.intros.luji.0.bio: He argues legitimacy with perfect posture, while a letter of surrender he dare not sign alone lies hidden in his sleeve.
story.shezhan.intros.luji.0.quote: Before resisting Cao, first answer me: what is a minister of Han?
story.shezhan.intros.yufan.0.bio: His words take no curve; the blade lands exactly where the opponent is most wretched.
story.shezhan.intros.yufan.0.quote: A man fleeing for shelter dares speak of saving others?
story.shezhan.intros.zhangzhao.0.bio: He remembers how you took his questions apart last time; this time he has stacked every canon into a wall of shields.
story.shezhan.intros.zhangzhao.0.quote: An allusion can be cited twice. Sir — can a string of defeats be answered twice?
story.shezhan.intros.zhangzhao.1.bio: Jiangdong's master of letters: he makes a city of the classics and peace his final gate.
story.shezhan.intros.zhangzhao.1.quote: Never mind arms for now. That Governor Liu has lost battle after battle — is it not fact?
story.shezhan.loss.clue: Lesson · The scholars question in rotation, turning a debate into attrition. Break the shared premise first. On retry, reading improves.
story.shezhan.loss.text: You answered every allusion point by point, but never made one of them admit to fear. All Sun Quan heard was a quarrel — and no one willing to own what resistance would cost.
story.shezhan.map.0.choices.0.detail: Reading improves; remember the shared premise
story.shezhan.map.0.choices.0.text: Press the question: 'after surrender, who owns Jiangdong's debt?'
story.shezhan.map.0.choices.1.detail: Scholars open with -1 morale; remember who signs
story.shezhan.map.0.choices.1.text: Ask each man of peace to write one word: surrender
story.shezhan.map.0.lines.0.text: Master Zhang asks who is stronger; Master Lu asks what is legitimate. I ask only this: a man chased as far as Xiakou — on what ground does he talk of saving anyone?
story.shezhan.map.0.lines.1.text: Chancellor Cao serves the Son of Heaven and commands the unsubmissive. What you resist — Cao's army, or the court itself?
story.shezhan.map.0.lines.2.text: Three questions, one shared lock: each begins by making me admit I have already lost.
story.shezhan.map.0.title: The Guest House · Three Questions, One Lock
story.shezhan.objective: Take apart the retreat of 'surrender to Cao and keep Jiangdong,' and make Sun Quan hear the fear his ministers never say aloud.
